title: No sign-in, claim, session or API-token flow for authenticated mode; credential carriage is undefined
evidence: docs/design.md:323-325 promises `authenticated` mode with a one-time claim URL and design.md:327 `FLEET_TOKEN` for scripts; status.proto:221 defines PRINCIPAL_KIND_API_TOKEN. But service.proto (all 189 lines) has no claim/login/logout/token RPC; 02b-hub-api.md:224-225 defers 'API tokens and user management' as an open question; 02b never mentions auth_mode at all (grep local_trusted/authenticated hits only design.md, common.proto:165-168, 04-technology-review.md:214). GetServerInfoResponse.caller is 'unset when not signed in' (common.proto:167-168) but nothing says how someone becomes signed in. 02b:204 lists UNAUTHENTICATED with no reason code. ADR 0016 (WebSocket attach) and 02b:176 never say whether credentials are a cookie, a bearer header, or a signed request.
problem: A React dashboard in authenticated mode cannot be built: there is no way to claim the first-admin URL, log in, hold a session across Connect unary + Watch stream + WebSocket attach, log out, or mint a CLI token. Browsers cannot set Authorization on a WebSocket, so the carrier choice (HttpOnly cookie vs token) changes the UI, CLI and Watch/attach handlers. There is also no User resource: Principal.id, Role assignment and `Device.principal_id` (device.proto:32) reference users the API cannot create or list.
fix: Add a short 'Authentication' section to 02b. It should say where the claim is handled (a fleetd command or plain HTTP, not FleetService) and how credentials are carried: browser = HttpOnly SameSite session cookie, which also covers the same-origin WebSocket upgrade; CLI/scripts = Authorization bearer token from FLEET_TOKEN. Keep token and user RPCs deferred under open question 1 (v3). Do not add an AuthService or new reason codes now.
verify: The gap is real but the severity is overstated. Confirmed: service.proto has no claim/login/logout/token RPC; design.md:323-327 promises the claim URL and FLEET_TOKEN; 02b has no auth section and never says how credentials ride Connect, Watch or the attach WebSocket (grep for cookie, bearer, ticket and Origin finds nothing in docs or api). However 02b:224-225 and ADR 0018:128 already list 'API tokens and user management as RPCs, or fleetd commands only' as an open question. design.md:425-439 puts login and browser attach in v3, and v1/v2 run on local_trusted. The first-admin claim can be a plain HTTP endpoint or fleetd command outside FleetService, so no proto change blocks v1/v2. Any RPCs are additive. The part that does matter now (principal and Origin rules in local_trusted) is covered under local-trusted-attack-surface.
resolution: New 02f-hub-authentication.md and hub/v1/auth.proto, token.proto: claim URL (first owner invite, fragment token, RedeemInvite), passkey Begin/Finish registration and login (WebAuthn JSON), GitHub sign-in as two redirect endpoints with a users-based allow-list, login sessions with an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, SignOut, Users and invites, API tokens (create once-shown, list, revoke); credential carriers per transport; GetServerInfo gains sign_in_methods and claim_pending; 17 RPCs added to service.proto; ADR 0019 addendum 10 to 12.

title: Watch: changing the filter is both 'resume with last token' and RESYNC_REQUIRED; pane-visible filtering has no grammar
evidence: 02b-hub-api.md:119-121 and watch.proto:2-3 and 04-technology-review.md Q5 say to change topics or filter 'the client reopens with its last resume_token'. 02b:129-130 puts a filter hash inside the token and 02b:134-136 says RESYNC_REQUIRED is sent 'when ... the filter differs from the token's'. ui-contract-map.md:95 and 02b:147-148 require PANE_SUMMARIES 'filtered to visible panes' (the 03g row 5 budget of 140 KB/s vs 2 MB/s). watch.proto:66-76 has one `filter` string for all topics, and 'Fields a topic lacks do not filter it'. No document lists filterable fields per Watch topic, and PaneKey is a 3-field message (ids.proto:91-101) with no string form, so `pane in (...)` cannot be written in the AIP-160 subset (02b:53-55). Only `session` is on PaneSummary (session.proto:96).
problem: Every scroll of the session sidebar changes the visible-pane set, which by 02b:134-136 forces a full RESYNC (all topics re-sent with send_initial) on the same stream that carries goals, triage and approvals. The two statements cannot both hold, and the one filter applied to all topics means a sidebar filter either leaks into goal/triage topics or is ignored by them. Latest-wins pane summaries are also not replayable from a change log, yet they share the resume machinery.
fix: The Subscription list is optional. Smaller fix: (1) the resume token's filter hash must exclude the PANE_SUMMARIES filter; (2) reopening with a changed pane filter sends INITIAL only for pane summaries and never RESYNC_REQUIRED, since summaries are latest-wins and not replayable anyway; (3) add a per-topic filterable-fields table to 02b, stating the pane filter is `session in (...)` or `machine = ...`. Do not fall back to a second stream per tab, because ADR 0016 keeps one stream per tab to stay under the HTTP/1.1 six-connection limit on local_trusted.
verify: The contradiction is confirmed. 02b:119-121, watch.proto:2-3, 04-technology-review.md Q5 and ADR 0016:30-32 all say a client changes topics or filter by reopening with its last resume_token. 02b:129-130 and 134-136 put a filter hash in the token and send RESYNC_REQUIRED when the filter differs. Watch is server-stream only because browsers cannot stream request bodies, so the sidebar's visible-pane filter (02b:147-148, ui-contract-map.md:95, 03g row 5) can only change by reopening. Every scroll would then force a full resync of all topics. watch.proto:66-76 has a single filter for all topics, and no per-topic filterable-field list exists. The pane grammar objection is overstated: PaneSummary has `session` and `machine` fields (session.proto:96-97), so `session in (...)` works (watch.proto:69-70). PaneKey has no string form.
resolution: watch.proto: WatchRequest now holds TopicSubscription{topic, filter, send_initial}; the token covers (topic, filter hash) per subscription, so a changed pane filter restarts only PANE_SUMMARIES and never sends RESYNC_REQUIRED (ResyncReason says why it is sent). 02c-hub-watch-and-filters.md has the rules, the AIP-160 grammar and the per-topic field catalogue (`session in (...)` for visible panes).

title: `version` bumps on every committed change, so expected_version is unusable on resources that carry live status
evidence: 02b-hub-api.md:84-85 'increases by 1 on every committed change to that resource; it is the resource's ETag' and 02b:86 'drop a Watch change whose (id, version) they already hold'. The same resources carry volatile fields: Machine.last_seen_time/load1/mem_available_bytes/battery (machine.proto:115,148-150); Device.last_seen_time (device.proto:39); Account.usage/pacing/probe refreshed by every probe (account.proto:124-126); Settings.generation/settings_epoch updated on delivery (settings.proto:61-62); Session panes' activity/last_output_time/attached_clients embedded in Session (session.proto:27-28,87). Writers take expected_version: UpdateMachine/DeleteMachine (machine.proto:185,222), UpdateAccount (account.proto:163), UpdateSettings (settings.proto:95), ApprovePairing/RevokeDevice (device.proto:68,84).
problem: A form loaded at version N will fail with VERSION_MISMATCH whenever a heartbeat, probe, delivery ack or pane tick lands in between, with no user-visible change. ApprovePairing/RevokeDevice on a phone that is pinging (last_seen_time) conflicts with itself. Conversely, if the hub avoids the bump to protect the ETag, the Watch dedupe rule (id, version) drops real status changes. One counter cannot serve both purposes. Watch MACHINES/ACCOUNTS/SESSIONS also become a heartbeat-rate firehose.
fix: Add one rule to 02b. Heartbeat- and probe-derived fields (last_seen_time, load1, mem, battery, clock_skew, device last_seen) are updated in memory, do not bump `version`, and reach Watch only on a state change or at most once per 30 s. State whether settings delivery acks (generation, epoch) bump Settings.version. No proto change.
verify: The ambiguity is real. 02b:84-90 bumps version on every committed change and dedupes Watch by (id, version). Machine carries last_seen_time, load1, mem_available_bytes and battery (machine.proto:115,148-150). Account carries usage, pacing and probe (account.proto:124-126). Device carries last_seen_time (device.proto:39). Settings carries generation and epoch updated on delivery (settings.proto:60-61). The docs never say whether these bump version. The impact is overstated. VERSION_MISMATCH with metadata current_version is retryable, and updates use field masks, so a retry is safe. Clients that follow Watch already hold the current version. Session has no expected_version writer. 03g row 3 and 03f:87 say heartbeats are latest-in-memory, 'last_seen write optional' and 'coalesced to the summary strip', so they likely do not reach Watch per heartbeat. A new `generation` field on every resource is not needed.
resolution: Every editable resource is split into spec (covered by version and expected_version) and status (observed_time, hub_seq, never versioned): Machine, Account, Goal, Session, Routine, Integration, Settings, Device. 02b "Versions and ETags" states that status and settings delivery acks never bump version; volatile status fields are coalesced (02c, "Volatile fields").

title: Scope model has no table for Watch topics, 'self' rules live only in proto comments, and READ is too broad for a phone
evidence: 02b-hub-api.md:144-145 only says 'Topics the caller cannot read are refused at open'; there is no topic-to-scope table for the 17 topics in watch.proto:23-44. Row-level rules are implied but not specified: ListDevices is ADMIN (service.proto:177-178) so WATCH_TOPIC_DEVICES needs ADMIN-or-self filtering; notification targets are 'own' (service.proto:181-188) so NOTIFICATION_TARGETS needs per-principal filtering; AUDIT, SETTINGS, OPERATIONS undefined. 'or the device itself' for GetDevice/RevokeDevice (service.proto:176,179) and [READ] on Create/Update/DeleteNotificationTarget (service.proto:183-188) are absent from the 02b scope table (02b:158-164). CreateNotificationTargetRequest carries a client-supplied `principal_id` (device.proto:141,168-171) with no 'server-set' rule. SCOPE_READ covers CapturePane, ReadSessionLog, AttachTerminal read-only, PaneSummary, Operation.output_text and GetAccount.include_raw_screen (service.proto:70,80-83; account.proto:148; common.proto:66) while ADR 0018:30-32 says the phone needs 'narrow scopes' to approve a prompt. Approvals and Triage are read through READ-scoped List/Get/Watch (service.proto:128-139).
problem: Implementers must guess authorization for Watch (the one stream carrying everything) and for the self-service RPCs; a viewer-level device could subscribe to DEVICES or other users' notification targets. A phone that only needs to see and decide approvals must hold READ and therefore can read every terminal screen and attach read-only, defeating the narrow-device goal. Adding a new scope later would silently change who can call ~20 RPCs.
fix: Add to 02b a Watch topic to scope table. The default is the scope of the matching List RPC. DEVICES is ADMIN or the caller's own device. NOTIFICATION_TARGETS is own rows unless ADMIN. Add the 'self' rules to the 02b scope table. Mark NotificationTarget.principal_id output-only: server-set from the caller and ignored on create. Note that a narrower approvals-read scope for the phone can be added later without breaking anyone, and defer it. Do not add SCOPE_READ_APPROVALS now.
verify: Partly confirmed. 02b:144-145 only says unreadable topics are refused at open, and no table maps the 17 topics (watch.proto:23-44) to scopes. DEVICES and NOTIFICATION_TARGETS need row-level rules, because ListDevices is [ADMIN] and notification targets are 'own' (service.proto:177-188). The 'self' rules appear only in service.proto comments, not in the 02b scope table (02b:158-164). device.proto:140-141 and 168-171 let the client set principal_id with no server-set rule. A Watch handler cannot be written without this. The READ-too-broad point is a real design concern but belongs to the phone (v3). Adding a narrower scope later is backward compatible if those RPCs accept READ or the new scope. Refactor risk is low, so 'high' is overstated.
resolution: New 02d-hub-authz.md: role to scope table, scope for every RPC (with self rules for devices and notification targets) and for all 17 Watch topics with row rules; service.proto notes [READ|APPROVALS], [self], [LOGS]; NotificationTarget.principal is output-only. A phone with only APPROVALS reads approvals, triage, the summary strip and its own operations; a separate approvals-read scope stays deferred as the finding proposed.

title: Roles and scopes are mixed: what Role does a narrowed device or token send to the agent, and which check wins?
evidence: Agent re-checks `requested_by.role` against command class and kind (02-contracts.md:186-187, 409, 416; command_goal.proto:160,189). Principal.role (status.proto:235) exists for every Principal; for kind DEVICE/API_TOKEN 02b:166 says only 'at most its user's scopes'. Role-based rules still appear in the hub API: KillWindowRequest 'needs ROLE_OWNER and an approval' (session.proto:245-246) while service.proto:76 labels KillWindow [SESSIONS_WRITE]; `Approval.required_role` (triage.proto:192-193) says 'Lowest role or scope' but the type is Role; PruneWorktree allow_dirty needs ROLE_OWNER (02-contracts.md:373 of 03c, 02-contracts.md:454).
problem: If the hub fills requested_by.role from on_behalf_of (the owner) a phone granted only SESSIONS_WRITE passes the agent's owner-only checks (developer KillWindow, allow_dirty), so narrowed scopes do not narrow what the agent allows. If it fills a lower role, there is no role for 'operator minus APPROVALS'. Approval.required_role cannot express a scope. Roles are documented as 'never compared numerically' but required_role/ROLE_OWNER are exactly role comparisons.
fix: Document in 02b that the hub sets requested_by.role to the highest role whose scope set is a subset of the caller's effective scopes. OWNER requires ADMIN, SETTINGS, APPROVALS and SESSIONS_WRITE, so a narrowed device or token is never OWNER. Reconcile KillWindow's label with its message comment (for example 'SESSIONS_WRITE, and a developer's window also needs an owner-level principal and an approval'). Fix the required_role comment to name roles only, or add `required_scope` as a new field and reserve nothing. Changing the field is unnecessary because it is additive.
verify: Confirmed. The agent re-checks requested_by.role against command class and kind (02-contracts.md:186-187, 409; command_goal.proto:160,189), and 02-contracts.md:454 requires ROLE_OWNER for KillWindow on a developer window and for allow_dirty. 02-contracts.md:336-343 and 02b:166 say a device or token acts on_behalf_of the owner with 'at most its user's scopes' but never say what Principal.role the hub sends for a narrowed DEVICE or API_TOKEN. If it copies the owner's role, narrowed scopes do not narrow the agent's checks. service.proto:76 labels KillWindow [SESSIONS_WRITE] while session.proto:245-246 says it needs ROLE_OWNER and an approval. triage.proto:192-193 says 'Lowest role or scope' but the field is a Role. The agent's role check is only 'defense in depth' (02-contracts.md:416-418), so the main enforcement is hub-side scopes, which makes this a doc and consistency gap rather than a wire blocker.
resolution: 02d "Role sent to the agent": the hub sends the narrowest role covering the effective scopes, OWNER only with SESSIONS_WRITE, APPROVALS, SETTINGS and ADMIN, so a narrowed device or token is never OWNER; hub scope check and agent role check both apply, stricter wins. Principal.role, KillWindowRequest and Approval.required_role comments reconciled (required_role is a role covered by the decider's mapped role).

title: local_trusted mode and WebSocket attach: no Origin/Host rules, no attach ticket, principal and auth_mode type undefined
evidence: design.md:323 `local_trusted` = hub on localhost, no login; ADR 0016:34 and 04-technology-review.md:237 define terminal attach as a WebSocket with input (terminal.proto:44-55 `bytes input`) but nothing specifies how it authenticates or checks Origin. 02b never mentions local_trusted, and design.md:318 says the hub listens only on the Tailscale interface and 'Browser terminal attach requires login', which contradicts local_trusted-on-localhost without a stated exception. GetServerInfoResponse.auth_mode is `string` (common.proto:165-166). No statement of which Principal (id, role, kind) a request has in local_trusted mode, though audit, Operation.requested_by, FLEET_OWNER and idempotency scoping (02b:69-70) all need a Principal.id.
problem: With no login, any web page the owner visits can open ws://localhost:<port> (WebSockets are not subject to CORS) or use DNS rebinding and type into the owner's tmux sessions and answer approvals: cross-site WebSocket hijacking is the main real-world attack on exactly this design. In authenticated mode the same applies to a cookie without CSRF/Origin checks. auth_mode as a free string will be wire-incompatible to change to an enum later.
fix: Document in 02b: local_trusted binds loopback only and refuses non-loopback addresses; every request and WebSocket upgrade passes a Host allow-list and same-origin Origin check; the fixed local principal is {id: "local-owner", kind USER, role OWNER}; attach in local_trusted follows the same Origin rule and design.md:318 is reconciled to 'login required in authenticated mode'. Change `auth_mode` to an enum (LOCAL_TRUSTED, AUTHENTICATED) before codegen. A CreateAttachTicket RPC is optional and can wait for v3.
verify: Confirmed. design.md:318-319 says the hub listens only on the Tailscale interface and browser attach requires login, while design.md:323-325 defines local_trusted as localhost with no login. 04-technology-review.md:214 contemplates plain-HTTP localhost and the attach WebSocket (ADR 0016:31-33) is specified without any authentication, Origin or Host check. common.proto:165-166 types auth_mode as a free `string`. The Principal used in local_trusted (audit, requested_by, FLEET_OWNER, idempotency scope at 02b:69-70) is never defined. Cross-site WebSocket hijacking and DNS rebinding are the standard attacks on a no-login localhost control plane that can type into tmux and answer approvals. In v2 the same applies to unary Connect calls that dispatch goals. Attach itself is v3 (design.md:439), but the Origin/Host rules and principal are needed for any v1 server. The string-to-enum change is wire-incompatible, so it is cheapest before codegen.
resolution: local_trusted binds loopback only and refuses other addresses; fixed principal local-owner (kind USER, role OWNER); Host allow-list, Origin check and no-CORS rules on every transport (02f); new HOST_NOT_ALLOWED and ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED reasons; CreateAttachTicket makes attach a second lock; AuthMode comments in common.proto; design.md reconciled to authenticated mode. (auth_mode was already an enum from theme A.)

title: Error model leaves common failures without reason codes; field-level validation and WebSocket errors unspecified
evidence: 02b-hub-api.md:197-206 table: `FAILED_PRECONDITION` includes 'machine offline for an attach' with no reason; NOT_FOUND and UNAUTHENTICATED reason '—' (02b:200,204); REASON_CODE_PAIRING_CODE_MISMATCH exists (status.proto:164-165) but is missing from the table; page_token 'valid for 10 min' (02b:52-53) and resume_token/filter/order_by parse failures have no stated code or reason; rate limits are 'per-principal' (02b:205) with no limit values in the spec or in GetServerInfo (common.proto:153-172). Precedence is unspecified when an approval is both stale and closed: DecideApproval uses expected_version (triage.proto:277-279) so a decided approval yields VERSION_MISMATCH or APPROVAL_CLOSED (02b:88-89,202). Attach errors: AttachClosed.reason is a free string (terminal.proto:81-83) and a WebSocket cannot carry a Connect error trailer.
problem: The dashboard cannot choose between 'sign in again', 'device revoked', 'machine offline', 'page expired, reload list', and 'someone else already decided', and cannot place form errors on fields. Two reasons (VERSION_MISMATCH vs APPROVAL_CLOSED) race for the phone's most important error.
fix: Only do the doc fixes now. Add PAIRING_CODE_MISMATCH to the 02b table, state that APPROVAL_CLOSED takes precedence over VERSION_MISMATCH on DecideApproval, and give a one-line code or reason for invalid page, resume and filter tokens. Leave the extra reason codes, WebSocket close codes and `limits` message for when the code needs them.
verify: Partly confirmed. REASON_CODE_PAIRING_CODE_MISMATCH exists (status.proto:164-165) but is absent from the 02b:197-206 error table. 'Machine offline for an attach' is listed under FAILED_PRECONDITION with no reason. Page, resume and filter parse failures have no stated code. When an approval is both stale and closed, VERSION_MISMATCH versus APPROVAL_CLOSED is unspecified (02b:88-89,202; triage.proto:277-279). AttachClosed.reason is a free string (terminal.proto:81-83). Most of the list is additive polish (new ReasonCode values can be added without breaking anything) and none blocks implementation. Rate-limit values belong in configuration.
resolution: status.proto: reason codes 506-520 (page, resume, filter, order, mask, request id missing, not found, exists, machine offline, credentials invalid and expired, goal phase changed, secret already delivered, field too large, pairing expired), FieldViolation and ErrorDetail.violations; AttachClosed carries reason enum plus ErrorDetail; 02b "Errors" has the full table, precedence (APPROVAL_CLOSED before VERSION_MISMATCH) and the WebSocket rules. Rate-limit values stay in hub configuration, not in GetServerInfo (deferred until code needs them).

title: Goal identity for hooks is bound by pane env or by cwd, and neither works for a reused session
evidence: 01d-goal-hooks.md:40-49 (Claude/Codex hooks gate on FLEET_GOAL_ID in the pane env; Muse gates on a cwd/session_id registry); 03c-goals.md:88-91 (FLEET_GOAL_ID is set only in the `ensure_window` step); 03c-goals.md:84-87 and command_goal.proto:109-113 (StartGoal can instead reuse an existing pane, so no ensure_window runs); 01-agent-capabilities.md:289-292 (E9 mapping is learned from hooks recording the session id against FLEET_PANE_KEY); events.proto:207-216 and snapshot.proto:194-214 (goal_id is carried on HarnessHookEvent, GoalState, PaneExited and PromptDetected with no stated source); 01d-goal-hooks.md:263-267 (open question about the registry only covers a goal that cd's away).
problem: Reuse of an available session is the steady-state dispatch path. A running harness process cannot gain a new env var, so in a reused pane FLEET_GOAL_ID is either absent (a session the developer marked available) or still the previous goal's id (a fleet-started session). Claude and Codex hooks therefore stay inert (no Stop guard, no E8 events), or events are attributed to the wrong goal. SessionStart already fired before the goal existed, so E9 (harness session id per pane) is never learned either. The Muse cwd registry has no lifecycle (when entries are removed, what happens when two goals share a checkout, reuse in REPO_DRIVER mode where the registered path is the main checkout and would capture every Muse session the developer runs there) and no wire representation, so the hub cannot see or reconcile it after an agent state loss.
fix: Decide that goal attribution is the agent's registry for all three harnesses, written by StartGoal before type_goal (new step register_goal) and removed on DONE/CLEARED/MERGED, pane exit or prune. Key it by (pane_key, worktree path, harness_session_id), learning the session id from the first UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse hook after registration. FLEET_GOAL_ID stays a fast path for new windows only. Add additive wire fields: a goal_binding source enum plus harness_session_id on PaneHarnessSession, and registered goals in Snapshot for hub reconciliation. Document registry behaviour for two goals sharing a checkout and for REPO_DRIVER mode (path is the main checkout), rather than hard-refusing it.
verify: Confirmed. 01d-goal-hooks.md:40-49 binds Claude/Codex hooks to FLEET_GOAL_ID in the pane env and Muse to a cwd registry. 03c-goals.md:84-91 sets FLEET_GOAL_ID only in ensure_window, and StartGoal.reuse_pane (command_goal.proto:109-113) skips that step. A running harness process cannot gain a new env var, so a reused pane has no goal id (marked-available developer session) or the previous goal's id. E9 (01-agent-capabilities.md:289-292) is learned from SessionStart against FLEET_PANE_KEY, which also predates the goal. grep of FLEET_GOAL_ID across docs/api finds no reuse-path handling. 01d:263-267 open question covers only a goal that cd's away. The Muse registry has no lifecycle and no wire field (snapshot.proto:115-140 has no binding). Reuse is the steady-state dispatch path (03c:70-71), so this blocks the central flow.
resolution: Goal identity is the agent's goal registry for all harnesses: new GoalRegistration, Snapshot.goal_registry, Event.goal_registry, RegisterGoal/ReleaseGoal, StartGoal step register_goal, TmuxPane.goal, PaneHarnessSession.goal/binding; FLEET_GOAL_ID is only a new-window fast path. Lifecycle, hook lookup order, two-goals-one-checkout and REPO_DRIVER rules in 02h; 01d and ADR 0019 item 17 updated.

title: Session reuse has no check that the pane is in the goal's repo or worktree
evidence: snapshot.proto:115-140 (TmuxPane has no cwd or repo); command_goal.proto:29-74 and :107-123 (GoalSpec.workdir, branch and worktree_mode, plus StartGoal.reuse_pane); 03c-goals.md:70-71 (planning rule: reuse any available session of the same harness on the machine); 03c-goals.md:84-87 (pick_session re-checks only idle, available and empty input line); 03c-goals.md:316 ('a session that was reused is left alone'); 01-agent-capabilities.md:293-306 (E11); status.proto:75-168 (no reason code for a workdir mismatch).
problem: The goal's worktree is ensured first, then a pane is reused whose harness process is fixed in a different cwd (typically the previous goal's worktree, possibly another repo). Claude and Muse cannot change directory (Codex has /cd). The goal would run in the wrong checkout, against the wrong branch, and Muse's cwd registry (01d) would not match. Neither PreflightResult.would_reuse nor any ReasonCode expresses this, and the hub cannot filter candidates because the agent never reports pane cwd.
fix: Add TmuxPane.current_path (tmux pane_current_path) plus a normalized RepoRef and worktree_path when under an allowed root, and REASON_CODE_SESSION_WORKDIR_MISMATCH enforced by pick_session and Preflight. Decide explicitly: reuse only when the pane's cwd is the goal's repo (worktree per session, branch switched in place), or only for harnesses that can /cd. Update planning rule 3 in 03c to match on repo.
verify: Confirmed. TmuxPane (snapshot.proto:115-140) has no cwd, repo or worktree path. 03c-goals.md:70-71 prefers any available session of the same harness on the machine with no repo match. pick_session (03c:84-87, diagram 03c:38) re-checks only idle, available_for_work and an empty input line. status.proto has no workdir-mismatch reason and PreflightResult.would_reuse cannot express it. A reused pane's harness process stays in its original cwd, so the goal would run in the wrong checkout or branch and the hub cannot filter candidates. This forces a decision on per-session vs per-goal worktrees (EnsureWorktree/PruneWorktree semantics) before implementation.
resolution: TmuxPane.workdir (PaneWorkdir{current_path, repo, checkout_path, is_worktree, branch, dirty}) plus hub Pane.workdir; reuse only when the pane is a clean checkout of the goal's repo, with REASON_CODE_SESSION_WORKDIR_MISMATCH and CHECKOUT_DIRTY from pick_session and Preflight.reuse_pane; planning rule 3 in 03c matches on repo (02h, Reuse).

title: The developer-keystroke signal that suppresses nudges and drives the typing banner has no wire carrier for goal panes
evidence: 03c-goals.md:272-273 and :367 (human_at_keyboard_until is set 10 min after AvailabilityChanged{reason='keystroke'}); 03-workflows.md:331; ui-contract-map.md:104 (banner 'you're typing into a running goal'); harness.proto:133-142 and 01-agent-capabilities.md:293-306 (Availability.idle requires 'no goal is active', so a goal pane is never idle); events.proto:229-238 (AvailabilityChanged is a from/to of Availability); events.proto:163-169 and snapshot.proto:115-140 (ActivityTransition and TmuxPane track output only, there is no last_input_at).
problem: A goal pane is never idle by definition, so no idle-to-busy transition, and therefore no 'keystroke' AvailabilityChanged, is ever emitted for it. The hub's rule to hold off nudges, goal control and the banner has no input. An Esc interrupt is also a keystroke; because the rule has no input, a goal the developer just interrupted looks like 'idle at ready prompt with WORKING line' and gets the corrective nudge (03c:284-296). tmux control mode also does not expose client input, so how the agent observes it is not stated.
fix: Add an additive per-pane input-activity signal: TmuxPane.last_input_at plus a COALESCE event (for example HumanInput{pane, at}), rate-limited, with the detection method specified (tmux client_activity polling or similar). Reword 03c:272 and 03-workflows.md:331 to consume it instead of AvailabilityChanged{keystroke}.
verify: Confirmed. Availability.idle requires no active goal (harness.proto:133-135, 01-agent-capabilities.md:293-295), so a goal pane is never idle and no idle-to-busy 'keystroke' AvailabilityChanged is emitted for it. Yet 03c-goals.md:272-273 and 03-workflows.md:331 derive human_at_keyboard_until and the nudge/goal-control suppression from exactly that event. TmuxPane has no last_input_at and no input event exists (grep for keystroke/last_input/HumanInput finds only the AvailabilityChanged reason string and the terminal stream). How the agent observes developer input is unstated. An Esc interrupt with no signal feeds the one-nudge rule (03c:284-296).
resolution: TmuxPane.last_input_time and Event.pane_input (PaneInput, COALESCE, at most one per 10 s) carry developer input on goal panes, with the detection method (tmux client_activity polling) in 02h; 03c, 03-workflows and 03f consume it instead of AvailabilityChanged{keystroke}.

title: Interrupt and pause have no wire representation, although 01d says they are reported as a HarnessCondition
evidence: 01d-goal-hooks.md:116-127 ('The agent reports HarnessCondition (E12) and the hub opens a Triage item goal interrupted'); harness.proto:199-213 (HarnessConditionKind: PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, USAGE_LIMIT, SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, NETWORK, OTHER); events.proto:197-204 (HookEventKind has no INTERRUPT, though Codex's Interrupt hook is the only hook signal); harness.proto:145-155 (GoalLineState has no PAUSED); 03c-goals.md:284-296 (idle with a WORKING line triggers the one-nudge rule); 01d-goal-hooks.md:23-24 ('never resume a goal the developer interrupted').
problem: An interrupted Claude goal ('Goal active', goal file still WORKING), a paused Codex goal, and a Muse 'goal paused by interrupt' are all indistinguishable on the wire from a stopped-without-DONE goal. The hub's nudge rule would type 'Your goal is still active. Continue' into a goal the developer deliberately stopped, which is the opposite of 01d. A native-/goal achieved or cleared state also has no field. The agent can only fall into OTHER or UNSPECIFIED.
fix: Add HARNESS_CONDITION_KIND_GOAL_INTERRUPTED (cleared when the goal runs again) and optionally HOOK_EVENT_KIND_INTERRUPT. Make 03c's stopped-without-DONE rule suppress on an open interrupted condition and map it to GOAL_PHASE_PAUSED with the 01d triage item. GOAL_LINE_STATE_PAUSED is optional.
verify: Confirmed. 01d-goal-hooks.md:116-127 says the agent reports an interrupt as a HarnessCondition (E12) and the hub opens a Triage item, and that nothing resumes automatically. HarnessConditionKind (harness.proto:199-213) has only PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, USAGE_LIMIT, SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, NETWORK, OTHER, and HookEventKind (events.proto:197-204) has no INTERRUPT (raw_event_name exists for unmapped kinds, which softens the hook half). GoalLineState has no PAUSED, and GOAL_PHASE_PAUSED (hub goal.proto:36-37) is set only by operator, review-loop cap or reserve rule. The stopped-without-DONE rule (03c-goals.md:284-296) suppresses only on provider_condition, prompt_pending and human_at_keyboard, so a developer-interrupted Claude goal (Stop does not fire on Esc, 01d:116-120) would be nudged 'continue', contradicting 01d and the product ground rule.
resolution: New HarnessConditionKind GOAL_INTERRUPTED and GOAL_PAUSED with HarnessCondition.pause_cause, and HOOK_EVENT_KIND_INTERRUPT; 03c suppresses the nudge on an open condition and maps it to PAUSED{OWNER_AT_MACHINE} with a GOAL_PAUSED triage item. GOAL_LINE_STATE_PAUSED not added: the goal file still says WORKING.

title: The hub is told to check /goal subcommand support before sending, but the agent never reports it
evidence: 01b-harness-commands.md:116-117 ('the hub never sends one that isn't listed'); hub/v1/goal.proto:224-226 (ControlGoal 'fails with GOAL_SUBCOMMAND_UNSUPPORTED before sending'); hub/v1/goal.proto:195-212 (pause is Interrupt for Claude and /goal pause for Codex and Muse; resume is typed `continue` for Claude and /goal resume for Codex and Muse); harness.proto:32-46 (CatalogEntry has only name and class); snapshot.proto:82-108 (HarnessInfo has no goal-control field); 02-contracts.md:297 (capability names include `goal.start` and a stale `goal.stop`, none for goal control).
problem: Whether a harness version supports pause, resume, edit and clear, and whether pause means a subcommand or Interrupt, is hard-coded hub-side per harness name. A harness update that adds `/goal pause` to Claude, or drops one in Codex, is discovered only after a failed command, and the Claude resume text `continue` is an unversioned hub constant. The 'before sending' promise cannot be met.
fix: Either add an additive HarnessInfo goal-control summary (supported subcommands, pause/resume mode, resume text) filled by the adapter per version, or reword 01b:116-117 and goal.proto:224-226 to say the failure comes from the agent and the hub falls back. Remove `goal.stop` from 02-contracts.md:297 either way.
verify: The gap exists: 01b-harness-commands.md:116-117 says the adapter records supported subcommands and the hub never sends an unlisted one, and hub goal.proto:224-226 promises GOAL_SUBCOMMAND_UNSUPPORTED 'before sending'. But CatalogEntry (harness.proto:32-46) is only name and class, and HarnessInfo (snapshot.proto:82-108) has no subcommand field. Severity is overstated: a reactive path already exists (02-contracts.md:145 G4 returns GOAL_SUBCOMMAND_UNSUPPORTED from the agent; 03c-goals.md:371 falls back to Interrupt), and pre-send detection is an optimization. The stale `goal.stop` capability name (02-contracts.md:297; StopGoal removed per 02-contracts.md:469, command.proto:45) is confirmed.
resolution: HarnessInfo.goal_control (GoalControl: subcommands, pause_mode, resume_mode, resume_text, limit_resume_verified) in type/v1/harness.proto, shown as MachineHarness.goal_control; the hub keeps no per-harness table (01b, 03c, 02h). goal.stop was already removed from 02-contracts.

title: SendKeys is used for nudges, Claude resume and limit-wait resume, but its gating is tied to prompt answering and it lacks an idle check
evidence: command_tmux.proto:119-128 (SendKeys has only answering_prompt and require_empty_input_line); command_tmux.proto:168-171 and 01-agent-capabilities.md:337-338 (RunHarnessCommand requires 'ready pattern showing, never into a running turn'); 01-agent-capabilities.md:284-285 and snapshot.proto:97-98 ('send-to-pane is enabled only once prompt detection is verified'); design.md:416-417 (Codex and Muse waiting detection still open); 03c-goals.md:290-296 (corrective nudge via SendKeys for every harness); 02-contracts.md:364-366 (limit-wait resume `SendKeys{'continue'}` for Claude); hub/v1/session.proto:156-165.
problem: One untyped command serves three purposes with different safety needs. require_empty_input_line does not imply the harness is idle: in a running Claude turn the input line is empty and typed text is queued as the next message. If the send-to-pane gate is applied to SendKeys generally, nudges and resume are blocked for Codex and Muse until prompt detection is verified, although they depend on the READY parser, not PROMPT. If it is not applied, the gate protects nothing. 'Typed commands only' is weakest exactly where hub-authored free text is typed.
fix: Doc-first: state that the E6 verification gate applies only when answering_prompt is set and that text sends are gated by ParserFeature.READY. If wanted, add an additive require_ready_prompt flag on SendKeys (PANE_BUSY otherwise). A separate SubmitPrompt kind is optional.
verify: Partly confirmed. SendKeys (command_tmux.proto:119-128) has only answering_prompt and require_empty_input_line, with no ready-prompt check, whereas RunHarnessCommand requires the ready pattern (command_tmux.proto:168-171). 01-agent-capabilities.md:284-285 says send-to-pane is disabled until prompt detection is verified and design.md:416-417 leaves Codex/Muse waiting detection open, so it is unstated whether nudges and the Claude limit-wait resume (02-contracts.md:364-366) are gated by E6 or only by READY. The input line is empty during a running Claude turn, so require_empty_input_line is not an idle check. Impact is small: the hub decides on an idle+ready transition first and a stray nudge becomes a queued message, so this is a clarification rather than a refactor driver. Hub SendKeysRequest (session.proto:156-165) mirrors the same fields.
resolution: SendKeys.purpose (SendKeysPurpose: PROMPT_ANSWER, GOAL_NUDGE, GOAL_RESUME, OPERATOR_TEXT) replaces require_empty_input_line; the E6 gate applies only to prompt answers, text sends need the READY parser, ready pattern showing and an empty input line (PANE_BUSY). Hub SendKeysRequest is OPERATOR_TEXT; 02g matrix rows split per purpose.

title: SetSessionAvailability addresses a tmux session but availability is a per-pane fact
evidence: command_tmux.proto:192-200 (SetSessionAvailability{SessionTarget session}); snapshot.proto:135 (TmuxPane.availability) and events.proto:229-238 (AvailabilityChanged.pane); 01-agent-capabilities.md:264-269 (windows are named by purpose, e.g. `codex prompt 1`, `claude w2`, `btop`, in one session); 01-agent-capabilities.md:297-300 (the developer marks 'it' available); hub/v1/session.proto:90 (sessions hold several windows and panes).
problem: A developer's tmux session usually holds several windows (several harnesses, btop). Marking the session cannot say which pane to treat as free capacity, and a mark on a session with two Claude panes is ambiguous. The spec also does not say where the mark persists (agent state across restart, pane respawn, tmux server restart changing server_start_id) or who re-asserts it on reconnect, though principle 1 puts desired state on the hub.
fix: Make the target oneof {SessionTarget session; PaneKey pane} (prefer pane) on both the agent command and the hub API. Specify that the agent persists marks in its state dir keyed by pane key and server_start_id, drops them when the pane dies, and reports them in TmuxPane.availability on every snapshot so the hub can re-send missing ones.
verify: Confirmed. SetSessionAvailability targets a SessionTarget (command_tmux.proto:192-200; hub SetSessionAvailabilityRequest session.proto:220-225) while availability lives per pane (TmuxPane.availability snapshot.proto:135, AvailabilityChanged.pane events.proto:229-238). Windows hold mixed purposes (01-agent-capabilities.md:264-269), so marking a session cannot identify the pane to use. The hub keeps available_for_work per session (03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:192). Where the mark persists across agent restart, tmux restart (server_start_id) or pane respawn is unspecified; 03d:205 says only that the command is declarative. Changing the target shape is cheapest before implementation.
resolution: SetSessionAvailability renamed SetPaneAvailability and addresses a PaneKey (agent command, hub RPC, OperationKind); reason is the enum AvailabilityReason. The agent persists marks per pane key in its state dir, drops them with the pane and reports them in TmuxPane.availability so the hub re-sends missing ones (02h, 03d).

title: Durable preflight reasons clear 'on the next snapshot or event', but forge CLI status and folder trust have neither
evidence: 03c-goals.md:117-121 (machine marked unfit for PUSH_ACCESS_MISSING, FOLDER_UNTRUSTED etc. 'until the next snapshot or event changes the fact'); snapshot.proto:361 and :263-278 (ForgeCliStatus and RepoAccess exist only in Snapshot.forge_cli); events.proto:40-102 (no forge-status or trust event); 01-agent-capabilities.md:97 and :376-378 (H4 is kind S only, cached 1 h); 03c-goals.md:64-65 (planning rule 3 reads ForgeCliStatus.signed_in and push_access); snapshot.proto:82-108 (HarnessInfo carries no folder-trust fact).
problem: Snapshots are sent only on connect or SnapshotRequest, and a healthy agent can stay connected for weeks. After the owner runs `gh auth login` or fixes repo access, the hub's copy stays stale and the machine remains unfit for that harness/repo. FOLDER_UNTRUSTED has no observable fact at all on the wire. The same stale copy also lets the hub plan onto a machine whose gh token has expired, wasting a dispatch.
fix: Either add an additive Event.forge_cli_status (COALESCE per host) sent when the agent's hourly H4 re-check changes, or add a hub rule that re-runs Preflight or SnapshotRequest for durable-unfit machines at a fixed interval. The re-check rule also covers FOLDER_UNTRUSTED, which has no event. Fix the 03c:120 wording to match whichever is chosen.
verify: Confirmed. ForgeCliStatus/RepoAccess exist only in Snapshot.forge_cli (snapshot.proto:263-278, :361); the Event body oneof (events.proto:40-102) has no forge-status or folder-trust event, and H4 is kind S only (01-agent-capabilities.md:97). 03c-goals.md:117-121 (and command_goal.proto:102-103) mark a machine unfit for durable reasons 'until the next snapshot or event changes the fact', but snapshots are sent only on connect or SnapshotRequest, and nothing in the docs triggers a re-check for a durable-unfit machine (grep of SnapshotRequest reasons shows only event_gap and slot_mismatch). FOLDER_UNTRUSTED has no observable fact anywhere on the wire. Recovery after `gh auth login` therefore depends on a reconnect or an operator retry, which undercuts the 'minimal owner attention' goal.
resolution: events.proto: new Event.forge_cli_status (54, COALESCE "forge:<tool>:<host>") sent when the hourly H4 re-check changes; hub re-runs Preflight for durably unfit (machine, harness, repo) after 10 min doubling to 1 h (this is how FOLDER_UNTRUSTED clears) and treats a ForgeCliStatus older than 2 h as unknown. 02i "Durable facts", 03c:138-145, 01 H4.

title: The StartGoal composite step list and its retry/idempotency classification omit steps that GoalSpec and 01d require
evidence: command.proto:96-98 and 03c-goals.md:82-91 (steps: preflight, ensure_worktree, pick_session, ensure_window, wait_ready, type_goal, confirm_goal_file); command_goal.proto:56-69 (model, effort, fresh_context via /model, /effort, /clear); 01d-goal-hooks.md:103-109 (agent writes the initial goal file just before type_goal); 01d-goal-hooks.md:44-49 (registry write at StartGoal); 01-agent-capabilities.md:412 and 346-360 (goal panes are always log-captured, G3 text does not mention model/effort/clear); 02-contracts.md:205-210 (crash-resume treats only preflight, worktree and window as declarative); status.proto:75-168 and :136-148 (no reason for an unavailable model or effort).

Per-step retry policy in 03c:117-126 is keyed on step names that do not cover them. A crash after `/clear` and before type_goal, or between writing the goal file and typing, has undefined behaviour.

Treat fresh_context as non-idempotent. Add REASON_CODE_MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE and REASON_CODE_EFFORT_NOT_SUPPORTED. Update the 03c retry table and the 02-contracts.md:205 resume rule.
verify: Confirmed gap, severity lowered. GoalSpec has model, effort and fresh_context (command_goal.proto:56-69, typed via /model, /effort, /clear), 01d-goal-hooks.md:103-109 has the agent write the goal file just before type_goal, and 01d:44-49 has a registry write. The step lists at 03c-goals.md:82-91 and command.proto CommandProgress.step comment do not name them (the proto comment says 'e.g.', so it is not exhaustive). The crash-resume rule at 02-contracts.md:205-210 classifies only preflight, worktree and window as declarative, so a crash after /clear (destructive) or after the goal-file write has no defined behaviour. status.proto has no reason for an unavailable model or effort (only FRESH_CONTEXT_NOT_ALLOWED at :146-148). title: The event delivery table covers 16 of 28 body kinds, and sequence gaps are ambiguous
evidence: events.proto:4-8 and :33-35 (class 'fixed per kind in 02-contracts.md'); 02-contracts.md:247-258 (the backpressure table lists pane_summary, resource_sample, spool_status, usage_reading, branch_state, probe_health, activity, prompt_detected/gone, harness_condition, local_approval, availability, goal_state, pane_exited, power_state, drain_state); events.proto:40-102 (unlisted bodies: account_identity, harness_changed, session_account_link, tmux_server, session, window, pane_created, harness_ready, harness_hook, pane_harness_session, repo, policy_changed); 02-contracts.md:212-214 (ring 'latest state per pane wins'); 02-contracts.md:256-257 (Heartbeat.event_seq reveals a gap that a SnapshotRequest repairs).

Because seq is assigned agent-wide and shed or coalesced events leave gaps, the hub cannot tell an expected SHED gap from a lost event, so a naive hub gap check would fire SnapshotRequest continuously under normal pane-summary shedding.

The table at 02-contracts.md:247-258 omits account_identity, harness_changed, session_account_link, tmux_server, session, window, pane_created, harness_ready, harness_hook, pane_harness_session, repo and policy_changed, although events.proto:4-8 and :33-35 say the class is fixed per kind there and the agent stamps Event.delivery and coalesce_key from it. 02-contracts.md:256-257 also says a shedding gap in Heartbeat.event_seq is visible and a SnapshotRequest repairs it, which conflicts with 03-workflows.md:255-262 (gap from ring overflow), leaving it unstated whether shed events consume seq numbers. Doc-only fix, low risk.
resolution: New docs/specs/02i-delivery-and-sequencing.md holds the class and coalesce_key of every Event body (31 kinds) plus the queue/ring rule per class and states that every event consumes a seq; events.proto body comments name each class, and 02-contracts.md points to 02i instead of its short table.

title: AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM is an 'interim CommandResult', contradicting 'exactly one CommandResult' and ResultAck
evidence: status.proto:64-65 (STATUS_AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM); 02-contracts.md:171 ('exactly one CommandResult') and :328 ('interim; a final result follows'); 02-contracts.md:157 (L3 carried as Status in CommandResult); agent.proto:258-261 (ResultAck lets the agent forget a result); command.proto:92-110 (CommandProgress already has status, reason and message); events.proto:252-261.
problem: If the interim state is a CommandResult, the hub's ResultAck, outbox transition to done and the agent's 'known command_id returns its logged result' rule would treat it as final, and the later real result would be a second result for the same command_id. The pending deadline and who must approve are not carried.
fix: Carry the interim state as CommandProgress{step:'awaiting_local_confirm', status: AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM} with the deadline in metadata. Keep CommandResult single and terminal, and mark AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM as progress-only in the status pairing table and in 02-contracts.md:157.
verify: Confirmed contradiction. 02-contracts.md:171 says the agent sends exactly one CommandResult, and 02-contracts.md:157 (L3) and :328 carry AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM as an interim Status 'in CommandResult' with a final result to follow. status.proto:64-65 defines it as a Status value. ResultAck (agent.proto:258-261) lets the agent forget results, so treating the interim as a result is ambiguous. CommandProgress (command.proto:92-110) already carries status, reason, message and metadata and is the natural carrier. The fix is small and additive.
resolution: AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM is now progress only: CommandProgress{step "awaiting_local_confirm", step_index 0, deadline in metadata}; CommandResult stays single and final. Fixed in status.proto, command.proto, 02-contracts (L3 row, error table, envelope checks), 02g, 02h and 01c.

title: Hook trust is a Codex-only bool with no unknown state, and several contract names have no capability behind them
evidence: harness.proto:56-58 (trust_pending 'Codex only'); 01d-goal-hooks.md:86-97 (Muse needs the same approval, `muse plugins approve`); events.proto:207-216 (HarnessHookEvent has no stop-guard decision or stop_hook_active, though 01d:18-22 says the guard 'refuses and escalates'); agent.proto:141 (CONNECT_REASON_HUB_REQUESTED, no hub message that requests a reconnect); events.proto:203 (HOOK_EVENT_KIND_GOAL_WRITTEN, but 01d:106-109 says the agent writes the goal file and hooks only read it); 02-contracts.md:297 (capability `goal.stop`); command_tmux.proto:135-143 and 01-agent-capabilities.md:158 (ResumeArgs use `--last`, RespawnPane carries no harness session id); snapshot.proto:159 and streams/LogStreamKey (agent cannot fill session_id for the developer's own sessions).

Stop-guard blocks cannot be audited or distinguished from a guard that never fires, which 03c:284-287 treats as a finding. Respawning with `--last` can resume the wrong conversation when several sessions share a cwd, though E9 already knows the session id. A log stream for a developer session has an empty session_id and must be keyed by pane.

Optionally add HarnessHookEvent.decision and an optional harness_session_id on RespawnPane and EnsureWindow. Leave the LogStreamKey item as a doc note.

HOOK_EVENT_KIND_GOAL_WRITTEN (events.proto:203) has no producer because 01d:103-109 has the agent write the goal file. CONNECT_REASON_HUB_REQUESTED (agent.proto:141) has no hub message that requests a reconnect (grep finds only the enum). RespawnPane (command_tmux.proto:137-143) carries no harness session id while resume uses `--last` (01-agent-capabilities.md:158), which can pick the wrong conversation.
