The LogStreamKey session_id point is weak: snapshot.proto:159 says session_id is empty for the developer's own sessions, but 02b-hub-api.md:28 says the hub assigns an id to every observed session.
resolution: GoalHooksState.trust is the tri-state HookTrustState (UNKNOWN, PENDING, TRUSTED, NOT_REQUIRED) with trust_approve_command; removed HOOK_EVENT_KIND_GOAL_WRITTEN and CONNECT_REASON_HUB_REQUESTED; added HarnessHookEvent.decision and harness_session_id on RespawnPane and EnsureWindow. The LogStreamKey item stays a doc note and belongs to theme D (dev-session-log-key).

title: Watch has one filter for all topics, and changing the filter contradicts RESYNC rules; pane-summary subscription cannot work as designed
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/watch.proto:66-76 (WatchRequest has one `filter` applied to every topic; 'Fields a topic lacks do not filter it'); watch.proto:3-4 and docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:121 ('to change topics or filter the client reopens with its last resume_token') versus 02b-hub-api.md:135 and watch.proto:57-60 (RESYNC_REQUIRED when 'the filter differs from the token's'; resume_token is 'hub instance, hub_seq, filter hash', 02b:128). docs/specs/ui-contract-map.md:29 and :95 (each view opens ONE Watch and PANE_SUMMARIES is 'filtered to visible panes'). mockup/view-session.js sidebar lists every window (needs all SESSIONS) while previews are for visible panes only.
problem: (1) The spec says both that reopening with a changed filter resumes and that a changed filter forces RESYNC_REQUIRED. Visible panes change on every sidebar scroll or session switch, so every navigation would force a full re-send (send_initial) of every topic. (2) One filter string across 17 topics cannot express 'all sessions, all goals, all triage, but summaries only for these 8 panes'. A filter such as `session in (...)` also drops triage items with an empty session (pacing items) and ignores topics without that field. (3) PaneSummary is Watch-only (02b:30), so there is no other way to fetch a preview.
fix: Decide before codegen. Minimum: fix 02b:121 and watch.proto:3-4 so a changed topics or filter always means a new stream with send_initial and no token (the hash only protects resume with the same filter). Then either (a) add per-topic filters (`repeated TopicSubscription{topic, filter}`, keeping `filter` as default), or (b) move PANE_SUMMARIES out of Watch into its own latest-wins server stream such as WatchPaneSummaries{repeated PaneKey} with no resume token, and state that the ui-contract-map views open one durable Watch plus one summaries stream. Both are additive.
verify: Contradiction confirmed: docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:120-121 and watch.proto:3-4 say a client changes topics or filter by reopening with its last resume_token, but 02b:128-129 puts a filter hash in the token and 02b:134-136 makes a differing filter RESYNC_REQUIRED. WatchRequest (watch.proto:66-76) has a single `filter` for all topics, and 'Fields a topic lacks do not filter it'. ui-contract-map.md:29 and :95 say one Watch with 'filtered to visible panes', PaneSummary is Watch-only (02b:29, no Get/List in service.proto). A `pane in (...)` filter would also filter Goal, which has a `pane` field (goal.proto:16). Not a blocker: a client can open two Watch streams (02b:119 says 'one server stream per client view', not one per client), and the contradiction is fixable in the spec before codegen. The claim that every navigation forces a send_initial of every topic holds only if one stream carries both.
resolution: Per-topic subscriptions in WatchRequest (see watch-filter-resume-contradiction); filter is validated against the topic, so a sidebar filter cannot leak into goals or triage; PANE_SUMMARIES stays on the same stream and is never replayed; CHANGE_TYPE_UNMATCHED added for resources that leave a filter.

title: Goal run history and timeline are stored by the hub but exposed nowhere: no start/end time, restarts, usage consumed, transcript or transitions
evidence: docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md:105 and 03c-goals.md:339 persist `goal_transitions` and `goal_runs` (nudges, restarts, usage consumed from readings, transcript path); docs/design.md:200 (Session view: 'run history per goal (restarts, nudges, usage consumed, transcript path)'); docs/specs/ui-contract-map.md:168 (Machines 'timeline of which goal ran where (7 days)' = `ListGoals{filter: create_time}`); api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:57-107 (Goal has only the latest `phase`/`phase_time`, `nudges`, `no_progress_runs`; no `start_time`, `end_time`, `restarts`, usage or transcript fields). api/fleet/hub/v1/session.proto:72-92 (Session has no state or end_time).
problem: A timeline bar needs when a goal started and ended, but `create_time` is plan time, and `phase_time` is overwritten (MERGED is replaced by CLOSED after merged_grace). A goal that ran in the window but was created before it is invisible to a create_time filter. There is no way to read the per-goal transition list or the run summary. Session carries no lifecycle, so the UI cannot tell a live session from an ended one. The 'Goal progress' task list is 'not in the contract (mock only)' (ui-contract-map.md:126); decide whether it is dropped or added.
fix: Additive. Goal: start_time (first RUNNING), end_time, restarts, usage_consumed (bucket key and percent points), transcript LogStreamKey. Add ListGoalTransitions{goal, page} returning {time, from, to, reason}. Let ListGoals filter on end_time or an active-between predicate. Add Session state/end_time only if the UI needs ended sessions. State in ui-contract-map whether 'Goal progress' is dropped. Medium priority: fits v2, but the Session view promise is in design.md.
verify: Confirmed. 03c-goals.md:339 and 03f-hub-internals.md:105 persist goal_transitions and goal_runs (nudges, restarts, usage consumed, transcript path). design.md:200 promises 'run history per goal (restarts, nudges, usage consumed, transcript path)' in the Session view. goal.proto Goal (lines 57-107) has only phase/phase_time, nudges, no_progress_runs and review_rounds; a grep for start_time, end_time, transcript, usage_consumed and restarts in goal.proto and session.proto finds nothing. ui-contract-map.md:168 builds the Machines timeline from ListGoals{filter: create_time}, which is plan time and misses goals created before the window that ran inside it. No RPC lists transitions (service.proto:88-96).

title: Session-log management API missing: no list of stored logs, delete, search, store usage or retention setting, and no read path for archived pane summaries
evidence: docs/adr/0010-session-logs.md:38-45 (UI search across sessions, per-session delete as one audited action, size cap with 'UI show usage'); docs/adr/0015-session-logs-in-sqlite.md ('Per-session delete is one transaction, audited'; 50 GB default size cap; pane summaries moved to logs.db at session end); docs/specs/03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:288 and 03f-hub-internals.md:111 (`log_sessions{session, machine, goal, bytes, first_at, last_at}`); api/fleet/hub/v1/service.proto:83 (only `ReadSessionLog`), service.proto has no list/delete/search/stats RPC; api/fleet/hub/v1/settings.proto:31-45 (HubSettings has no log size cap or retention); `spool_cap_bytes` (type/v1/settings.proto:80) is the agent spool, not the hub store; 02b-hub-api.md:30 (PaneSummary 'Watch only'); mockup/view-session-panels.js:33-45 (replay, search, sizes shown as placeholders).
problem: ReadSessionLog needs a LogStreamKey, which a client can only learn from live `Session.logs[]`. Once a session or window is gone, or a goal has ended, nothing lists its logs, although `log_sessions` is kept. `fleet logs export <session>` therefore cannot discover what to export, and 'load it later to research' has no entry point. There is no DeleteSessionLogs (audited), no search (ADR 0010 requires it; nothing says how zstd chunks are searched), no hub log-store status (bytes used, cap, oldest, days retained, paused-for-disk), and no setting for the cap or retention. The owner decision that pane summaries are archived at session end has no API to read them back.
fix: Additive RPCs: ListLogSessions (filter machine, goal, harness, time; returns key(s), bytes, first/last time, final), DeleteSessionLogs{session, request_id} (audited), GetLogStoreStatus (used, cap, oldest, paused). Add TRIAGE_KIND_LOG_DISK_LOW. Add log_size_cap_bytes to HubSettings. For search, either specify it (FTS or scan of zstd frames) or amend ADR 0010 to mark it a later non-goal. Archived pane summaries can ride in ListLogSessions as last_summary. Not v1; do it before v3 logs work, but decide search-or-defer in the docs now.
verify: Confirmed. service.proto:83 has only ReadSessionLog; ReadSessionLogRequest (terminal.proto:97) takes a key, which a client can only learn from live Session.logs[]. ADR 0010:38-45 requires search across sessions, per-session audited delete and 'UI show usage'; ADR 0015:42-45 adds the 50 GB cap and archives pane summaries to logs.db; 03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:338 raises triage `log_disk_low`, but triage.proto TriageKind (lines 18-40) has no such kind (only OTHER=63); HubSettings (settings.proto:30-45) has no log cap or retention; PaneSummary is Watch-only. ADR 0015:59 makes `fleet logs export <session>` the only way out, which needs a way to find the stream keys of ended sessions.

title: Logs are READ scope in the API but owner-only in ADR 0010; a viewer or phone device can read all terminal history
evidence: docs/adr/0010-session-logs.md:47-49 ('readable only by the hub user and people with the owner role', terminal output may contain tokens or secrets); docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:160 (SCOPE_READ allows 'logs, read-only attach, CapturePane' for viewer); api/fleet/hub/v1/service.proto:82-83 (`ReadSessionLog` is [READ]); service.proto:80-81 (read-only attach [READ]); api/fleet/hub/v1/common.proto:64-77 (Scope enum has no logs or sensitive-content scope); mockup/view-session-panels.js history text 'readable by owner only'.
problem: Scopes are sets handed to devices and API tokens, so the stated 'owner only' rule has no way to be expressed or enforced. Any READ-scope device pairs and reads every captured session, including the developer's own sessions with capture on, and `GetAccount{include_raw_screen}` (account.proto:148, [READ]) returns screen text with the same sensitivity.
fix: Pick one rule before codegen and write it in 02b and ADR 0010. Either add SCOPE_LOGS (owner role only by default, required for ReadSessionLog, log list/delete/search and include_raw_screen, and not grantable to a device unless the owner ticks it), or amend ADR 0010 to say READ includes logs and drop the owner-only claim. The enum addition is additive, so keep the severity at important, not blocker.
verify: Confirmed contradiction. ADR 0010:47-49: logs 'readable only by the hub user and people with the owner role'. 02b-hub-api.md:160 puts 'logs, read-only attach, CapturePane' in SCOPE_READ, held by viewer, operator and owner; service.proto:80-83 tags ReadSessionLog and read-only attach as [READ]; the Scope enum (common.proto:64-77) has no logs scope; GetAccountRequest.include_raw_screen (account.proto:148) is also READ-scoped. A viewer-role user or a READ-scope device can therefore read every stored terminal stream.
resolution: common.proto: SCOPE_LOGS (owner only by default, never in a phone pairing request) required for ReadSessionLog and GetAccount.include_raw_screen and for archived pane summaries; roles map in 02d; ADR 0019 addendum records the rule.

title: Dispatch panel: PreflightGoal request is incomplete and the 'manual allowed with a warning' path (DISPATCH_CONFIRM) is unwired
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:176-181 (PreflightGoalRequest has work_item, repo, placement only) vs 151-167 (StartGoalRequest also has change_request, consent, goal_text, model, effort, fresh_context); goal.proto:170-173 (StartGoalResponse has no approval); api/fleet/hub/v1/triage.proto:138 (APPROVAL_KIND_DISPATCH_CONFIRM, 'confirm a manual dispatch the scheduler would refuse') is referenced by no request or response; goal.proto:183-192 (`hub_checks` are plain ErrorDetail with no severity); api/fleet/type/v1/status.proto:84-100 (ReasonCode 1..16 has DRAINING and SLOTS_FULL but nothing for reserve reached, ahead of pace, usage unknown, interactive-only/manual-only account, integration degraded, claimed elsewhere, repo not watched, work item already has a goal); docs/specs/03e-settings-and-drift.md:199 and 03c-goals.md:167 ('manual dispatch allowed with a warning'); mockup/fleet-dispatch.js:92-110 and 133 (any 'bad' reason disables Dispatch; the preview text depends on consent).
problem: The dispatch preview ('keys the agent will type') cannot reflect consent, goal text, model or effort edits because Preflight cannot take them; 'Drive to merge' for an unowned PR cannot preflight (no change_request). The contract promises manual dispatch past a warning but gives the client no way to tell blocking from warning checks, and no field to acknowledge them or to carry an Approval for the DISPATCH_CONFIRM kind, so the UI and CLI will each invent a rule. Pacing refusals have no stable reason codes, so the UI must string-match.
fix: Additive. Share one GoalSpecInput message between StartGoalRequest and PreflightGoalRequest (add change_request, consent, goal_text, model, effort, fresh_context to preflight). Add a PreflightCheck{ErrorDetail, severity BLOCK|WARN|INFO} list (deprecate hub_checks or keep it as the BLOCK subset). Add hub-rule ReasonCodes (pacing reserve, ahead of pace, usage unknown, account not dispatchable, work item claimed or busy, integration degraded, repo not watched). Add acknowledged_warnings to StartGoalRequest and an approval field to StartGoalResponse for DISPATCH_CONFIRM, and state that Operation is unset until it is decided. The Operation-versus-approval ordering for RunHarnessCommand/KillWindow is the same question; settle it in one rule in 02b.
verify: Confirmed. PreflightGoalRequest (goal.proto:176-181) has only work_item, repo, placement, while StartGoalRequest (151-167) also has change_request, consent, goal_text, model, effort, fresh_context. ui-contract-map.md:79 shows the 'keys the agent will type' preview from PreflightGoal, which cannot depend on edits it never receives. APPROVAL_KIND_DISPATCH_CONFIRM (triage.proto:135-138) is referenced nowhere else in api or docs (grep finds only its definition), and StartGoalResponse (goal.proto:170-173) carries no approval. hub_checks (goal.proto:189-191) are plain ErrorDetail with no severity, yet 03e-settings-and-drift.md:199 says manual dispatch is 'allowed with a warning'. ReasonCode (status.proto) has DRAINING and SLOTS_FULL but no pacing, usage-unknown, claimed or work-item-busy codes.

title: Per-repo settings (consent, parallel cap, tracker-to-repo mapping, hooks mode) have no home: Integration.watched is a list of strings
evidence: api/fleet/integration/v1/integration.proto:92-93 (`repeated string watched`), api/fleet/hub/v1/work.proto:157-164 (UpdateIntegration masks integration.watched); docs/adr/0008-goal-consent-and-account-modes.md:17-33 (consent configurable per repo, YAML `repos[].consent`); api/fleet/hub/v1/settings.proto:34 and 35-36 (max_parallel_goals_per_repo and default_consent are fleet-wide only); docs/design.md open question 'cap on parallel goals per repo'; docs/adr/0012-integration-model.md open question (how a Jira ticket names its target repo, per-project owner configuration); docs/specs/ui-contract-map.md:81 ('default repo ∩ account') and :177 (watched repos with host, provider, hooks); mockup/view-settings.js:12-13, 31-33 (per-repo hooks, host, provider).
problem: The effective-consent rule is repo ∩ account, but there is no repo-level consent to read or write. The parallel-goals cap is meant per repo but only a fleet-wide number exists. A Jira project or other tracker has to map to target repos, and that mapping has nowhere to live. A bare string also cannot carry enabled/paused or the code-host-vs-tracker distinction. Changing `watched` from string to a message later is a breaking Connect-JSON change for every client.
fix: Add `repeated WatchedSource watched_sources` to Integration with {path_or_project, enabled, consent, optional max_parallel_goals, target_repos, optional trusted_label}, keep `watched` as a deprecated mirror, point UpdateIntegration and ui-contract-map.md:81/177 at it, and write effective consent = source consent (else HubSettings.default_consent) intersect account consent. Alternatively add a repo settings layer in SettingsScope. Decide which before codegen; keep repo_ships_own read-only and derived.
verify: Confirmed. integration.proto:92-93 `repeated string watched`; UpdateIntegration masks only integration.watched (work.proto:157-158). ADR 0008:18-33 states consent is 'configurable per repo and per account', effective = intersection, with YAML `repos[].consent`, but HubSettings (settings.proto:34-36) has only fleet-wide default_consent and max_parallel_goals_per_repo, and SettingsScope (settings.proto:21-29) has only fleet, group and machine layers. design.md:401 and ADR 0012's open question leave the per-repo cap and tracker-to-repo mapping unplaced. Refactor risk is overstated: the fix is an additive field plus a deprecated `watched`, not a breaking change, but v2 needs per-repo consent (ADR 0008) and the proto gives it no place.

title: Accounts can only be updated, never created or removed; Codex mapping and API-key (OpenCode) accounts have no creation path and Account has no provider field
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/service.proto:116-122 (ListAccounts, GetAccount, UpdateAccount, ProbeAccount only); api/fleet/hub/v1/account.proto:156-164 (UpdateAccount can edit `bindings` 'to map a Codex account that shows no identity to a machine'); docs/specs/01-agent-capabilities.md:195-199 (Codex shows no identity, 'the owner picks the Codex account for each machine on the hub'); account.proto:99-129 (no `provider`; Pane has it, session.proto:39-41); mockup/fleet-data.js apiAccounts and mockup/view-usage.js:60-68 (API-key cards per provider: DeepSeek, Moonshot; chips by provider; spend cap); ui-contract-map.md:150-155 (cap and OpenCode rows).
problem: If Codex yields no AccountKey, there is no Account record to hold the owner's mapping, so UpdateAccount has nothing to update (a placeholder-per-machine rule is not written anywhere). API-key accounts (budget_kind DOLLAR_CAP, spend_cap_micros) are owner-defined, yet nothing creates them or says whether they are discovered from `opencode stats`. A stale or duplicate account (re-keyed after a salt change) cannot be deleted or merged. The hub cannot enforce 'never auto-dispatch OpenCode on an Anthropic subscription' without a machine-readable provider.
fix: Document in 03b the auto-created placeholder accounts (Codex per machine and profile) and discovery of API-key accounts. Add `provider` to Account and defer Create/Delete/Merge to a later additive change. Do not add CreateAccount for subscriptions.
verify: Partly refuted. The Codex mapping does have a record: 02-contracts.md:439 says the agent hashes "<harness>:<machine_id>" into an AccountKey with identity_not_shown, so the hub gets an Account per machine and the owner maps it via UpdateAccount bindings (account.proto:156-164). OpenCode providers are discovered from `opencode providers list` (01b-harness-commands.md:62). What is confirmed: no CreateAccount/DeleteAccount/MergeAccounts RPC (service.proto:116-124), no `provider` field on Account (account.proto:99-129; provider exists on Pane), and 03b does not write down the auto-create rule for Codex placeholders or API-key accounts. Merge/delete is polish for stale or re-keyed accounts, and the OpenCode-on-Anthropic rule can be enforced from the session-account link, so this does not block v1/v2.

title: `fleet export` / `fleet import --dry-run` and 'imported machines start drained' have no API; machine records cannot be pre-provisioned
evidence: docs/design.md:329-330 (`fleet export`/`import`: fleet.yaml, `--dry-run` first, imported machines start drained); docs/adr/0009-machine-groups-and-layered-settings.md:29 ('hub database / fleet.yaml'); mockup/view-settings.js:9-21 and fleet.yaml preview; api/fleet/hub/v1/service.proto (no export/import RPC); api/fleet/hub/v1/machine.proto:229-237 (CreateEnrollmentTokenRequest has machine_name, ttl, previous_machine only); docs/specs/03-workflows.md:99 (a machine row is inserted only at Enroll).
problem: A client could compose export from List/Get calls, but import is many non-atomic RPCs with no server-side diff, so `--dry-run` is not trustworthy and a partial failure leaves a half-applied fleet. Machine entries in fleet.yaml (labels, max_active/max_total, drained) cannot be applied before the machine exists, and the settings layer `machine/<id>` needs an id that is assigned at Enroll. The enrollment token cannot carry labels, initial settings, start_drained, or a separate expected hostname (machine_name is 'also the expected hostname', so renamed machines produce false hostname-mismatch warnings). Which of fleet.yaml and the database is the source of truth is also unstated (ADR 0009:29).
fix: Decide in docs now: either mark export/import as post-v2 and remove it from the v2 'fleet CLI contract', or specify server-side ExportConfig/ImportConfig(dry_run) returning a plan. State that the database is authoritative and fleet.yaml is an export/import format only. Token-carried labels/start_drained are optional and can wait.
verify: Confirmed that design.md:329-330 names `fleet export`/`fleet import --dry-run` and 'imported machines start drained', and service.proto has no export/import RPC, nothing in 02b or ADR 0018 mentions them, and CreateEnrollmentTokenRequest (machine.proto:229-237) has only machine_name, ttl and previous_machine. ADR 0009:29 does not say whether the database or fleet.yaml is authoritative. Still, export can be composed from List/Get, the gap is additive to fix, and `import` is a CLI convenience rather than a v2 blocker; the 'imported machines start drained' line is an inconsistency to resolve in the docs (machines exist only after Enroll).

title: CLI commands that must go through the hub (backup, API tokens and login bootstrap, store status, debug stream) have no RPC
evidence: docs/adr/0002-storage-sqlite.md:38 and docs/specs/04-technology-review.md:151,271 (`fleet backup`, `--include-logs`); docs/design.md:322-327 (first login via one-time claim URL; `FLEET_TOKEN` for scripts) and 432-437 (v2 includes 'the fleet CLI contract'); docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:222-224 (open question 1: tokens and users as RPCs or fleetd commands) and common.proto:Principal kind API_TOKEN (type/v1/status.proto:225-233); docs/adr/0003-transport-grpc.md:45 (`fleet debug stream` prints decoded messages); docs/adr/0018 ('CLI talks only to fleet.hub.v1'); api/fleet/hub/v1/service.proto (no backup, token, claim or store-status RPC).
problem: ADR 0018 says the CLI uses only FleetService, yet `fleet backup` and token creation are named CLI commands with no RPC. FLEET_TOKEN is in the v2 CLI contract, so the open question blocks v2: nothing mints, lists, scopes or revokes a token, and nothing defines the browser login or claim-URL exchange the 'authenticated' mode needs (GetServerInfo.caller exists but no way to become a caller). `fleet debug stream` is ambiguous: a Watch tap is covered, an agent-wire tap is not exposed. There is also no store status (state.db/logs.db size, last backup, schema version) for the Settings view or `fleet doctor`.
fix: Record in 02b that `fleet backup`, token/user administration and the claim URL are local `fleetd` subcommands for v1/v2 (or add StartBackup/GetStoreStatus later), and that `fleet debug stream` decodes a Watch tap only. Leave tokens as the existing open question until v3.
verify: Partly an explicit open question: 02b-hub-api.md:222-225 lists API tokens and user management as RPCs versus fleetd commands as open question 1, and auth, login and claim flows are v3 (design.md:436-437), with v2 running local_trusted. Confirmed leftovers: ADR 0002:38 and 04-technology-review.md:151,271 name `fleet backup` (and --include-logs) while ADR 0018:45-46 says the CLI talks only to fleet.hub.v1 and service.proto has no backup or store-status RPC; ADR 0003:45 names `fleet debug stream` with no decoded-stream interface. These are small decisions, not v2 blockers.

title: Nothing triggers or exposes EnsureGoalHooks: no reconcile step and no hub RPC, yet generic-hook repos depend on them
evidence: docs/specs/01d-goal-hooks.md:65 (`EnsureGoalHooks{harness, workdir, expected_version}`); docs/specs/03-workflows.md:125-132 (snapshot reconcile enqueues only EnsureProbe and SetLogCapture); docs/specs/03c-goals.md:122-127 and the StartGoal steps (preflight, ensure_worktree, pick_session, ensure_window, wait_ready, type_goal, confirm_goal_file) have no hooks step ('EnsureGoalHooks suggested'); docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:90-103 (hub RPC to agent command table has no EnsureGoalHooks); api/fleet/hub/v1/service.proto (no RPC); mockup/view-machines.js:21-26 ('reinstall on the machine') and view-settings.js:44-47 (generic: EnsureGoalHooks installs the fleet hooks).
problem: The Machines view shows hook state and the Settings view says generic repos get fleet hooks via EnsureGoalHooks, but no component is specified as sending it (not at enroll, not on harness change, not before a goal) and the owner has no way to request install or re-verify from the UI or CLI. Without hooks the stuck/done detection and the Muse goal registry (01d) are absent in v2. `fleet-agent hooks uninstall` is local-only, which is fine, but install is not.
fix: Add a reconcile rule in 03-workflows (W1/W11) that enqueues EnsureGoalHooks per (harness, profile, watched checkout) when GoalHooksState is missing, unverified or version-behind, never over a running goal. Add an owner-triggered RPC such as EnsureMachineHooks{machine, harness, profile} returning an Operation (SCOPE_SETTINGS) and list it in 02b. Add the Muse registry write to the 03c StartGoal step list.
verify: Confirmed. EnsureGoalHooks exists on the agent wire (command_goal.proto:170-179, 02-contracts.md:142) and 01d-goal-hooks.md:65 defines it, but the snapshot reconcile (03-workflows.md:125-132) enqueues only EnsureProbe, goal and orphan handling, and 03c-goals.md:126 only says 'EnsureGoalHooks suggested' on GOAL_FILE_NOT_SEEN. 03e-settings-and-drift.md:188 re-verifies hooks 'on the next EnsureGoalHooks' with no sender specified. 02b-hub-api.md:90-111 has no hub RPC mapping to it and service.proto has none, while mockup/view-machines.js shows 'reinstall on the machine'. The Muse goal registry write is described only in 01d:47, not in the 03c StartGoal steps. Hooks are optional per design.md:76 ('A worker without hooks still shows up'), which keeps this from being a blocker.

title: `version` as ETag covers volatile status on Machine, Account and Goal, so expected_version fails constantly
evidence: docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:70-77 ('version ... increases by 1 on every committed change to that resource'; expected_version mismatch is FAILED_PRECONDITION); api/fleet/hub/v1/machine.proto:106-154 (Machine mixes editable `display_name`/`labels` with `load1`, `mem_available_bytes`, `battery`, `slots`, `last_seen_time`); account.proto:100-129 (editable reserve/consent/mode next to `usage`, `pacing` rewritten every evaluation, docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md:90 and 03b-usage-and-sync.md:137); goal.proto:57-107 (ControlGoal takes expected_version; Goal carries first_line, head_commit, dirty); ui-contract-map.md:71 (UpdateAccount from Settings).
problem: The owner edits a reserve or label with the version they last saw; any pacing re-evaluation, heartbeat-driven telemetry, or goal-line change in between bumps `version`, so the write fails with VERSION_MISMATCH although no editable field changed. Heartbeat-fed fields on Machine also make every Watch MACHINES update carry the full resource (catalog entries, repos, effective settings) at the heartbeat rate, which 03g (row 3) assumed would be coalesced into the summary strip only.
fix: Write one rule in 02b before codegen: either add config_version (bumped only by Update RPCs) to Machine, Account, Goal, Routine and Integration and define expected_version against it, or state that version bumps only on persisted-resource content change and that heartbeat-fed fields (load1, mem, battery) and unchanged pacing never bump it nor produce a Watch update except on state transitions or at most once a minute.
verify: Confirmed ambiguity. 02b-hub-api.md:84-87 defines version as increasing on every committed change and the ETag for expected_version; Machine (machine.proto:106-154) mixes editable display_name/labels with load1, mem_available_bytes, battery and slots, and Account embeds pacing, which 03b-usage-and-sync.md:137 says is rewritten per scheduler evaluation. 03g-load-and-handoff.md:30 treats heartbeats as can-lose, in-memory and coalesced, so it is unspecified whether heartbeat-fed fields bump version or are emitted on Watch MACHINES at heartbeat rate. The failure case (UpdateAccount failing with VERSION_MISMATCH after an unrelated pacing rewrite) is plausible but not certain; the 'high refactor risk' rating is overstated because config_version is additive.
resolution: Same spec/status split as version-etag-vs-volatile-fields: Machine telemetry, Account usage and pacing, Goal phase and goal-file facts are status; ControlGoal gets expected_phase (GOAL_PHASE_CHANGED) next to expected_version, which now covers the spec (EDIT).

title: Smaller mismatches: audit filter lacks target/session, read-only toggle has no wire message, machine labels ambiguity, next-up ordering
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/settings.proto:129-131 (ListAuditEntries filter fields: actor.id, action, machine, goal, create_time) vs docs/specs/ui-contract-map.md:130 (`filter: target or machine`); AuditEntry (settings.proto:106-127) has no session or pane field; mockup/view-machines.js audit header shows 'N entries' (List responses carry no total). api/fleet/hub/v1/terminal.proto:19-25 and agent/v1/streams.proto:66-79 (read_only is fixed at open; no mode message) vs mockup/view-session-tmux.js:50-52 ('Read-write' / 'Read-only' button toggles during a session). machine.proto:130 (`labels` = effective: hub-assigned plus local) vs 180 (UpdateMachine edits labels 'hub-assigned only'). docs/specs/ui-contract-map.md:74 ('Next up' via PreflightGoal) vs work.proto:91-98 (ListWorkItems has no order_by or filter for READY order) and mockup/view-work.js nextUp().
problem: (1) The Session Timeline cannot query audit by session or target as the map claims; define which `target` each action writes (e.g. `sessions/<id>`) and add it and `session` to the filter list, plus an optional `total_size` on List responses. (2) The attach read-only switch needs either a reattach or a new message. (3) Writing back an effective label list would try to store local labels as hub labels. (4) 'Next up' needs the scheduler's READY order, which no field or order_by exposes.
fix: Add `target` to the audit filter fields and document which target each action writes (for example sessions/<id>). State that toggling read-only reattaches. Clarify that UpdateMachine ignores local labels or split hub_labels/local_labels. Document that 'next up' is PreflightGoal with an empty placement; skip queue_rank and total_size until a view needs them.
verify: Confirmed in part. ListAuditEntriesRequest filter fields (settings.proto:129-131) are actor.id, action, machine, goal, create_time, while ui-contract-map.md:130 says `filter: target or machine`; AuditEntry.target is '<collection>/<id>' (settings.proto:112) so it is easy to add to the filter list. The AttachOpen read_only flag (terminal.proto:24) is fixed at open and the mockup has a toggle, so a re-attach rule is needed. Machine.labels is 'effective' (machine.proto:130) while UpdateMachine edits 'hub-assigned only' (line 180). The 'next up' order has no field in ListWorkItems (work.proto:91-98). The total_size and queue_rank asks are speculative.

title: Reused-session goals cannot get FLEET_GOAL_ID or the right cwd, so hooks, goal registry and adoption all break on the reuse path
evidence: 03c-goals.md:70-72 makes reusing an available_for_work session the preferred plan ('reuse (no new window)'); 03c-goals.md:87-91 says FLEET_GOAL_ID/FLEET_PANE_KEY are put in the pane environment by ensure_window, a step that is skipped on reuse (command_goal.proto:109-123 reuse_pane, in_session). 01d-goal-hooks.md:40-43 states Claude/Codex hooks gate on FLEET_GOAL_ID reaching hooks through the pane environment; a harness process already running cannot receive a new env var. W2 adoption/orphan detection (03-workflows.md:130-131, 03c-goals.md:243 PANE_LOST->RUNNING 'same FLEET_GOAL_ID') and snapshot.proto:126-128 TmuxPane.fleet_tags depend on the same tag. 01d-goal-hooks.md:44-49 (Muse registry keyed by worktree cwd) and 01d:263-267 (open question) never say what cwd a reused session has: the reused harness is sitting in whatever directory it was started in, not the new goal's worktree (WORKTREE_MODE_AGENT_ENSURES, command_goal.proto:20-26). In WORKTREE_MODE_REPO_DRIVER the goal starts in the main checkout, so registering that path makes every developer Muse session in the same checkout look like a fleet goal (Stop guard fights the developer). problem: The identity of a fleet goal on the machine is defined three incompatible ways (env var, cwd registry, session_id) and the registry has no lifecycle: no write step in StartGoal, no persistence entry, no release trigger, no rebuild rule after state-dir loss or re-enroll, no reconcile visibility on the wire. The reuse path (the main way to keep subscriptions busy) cannot satisfy any of the three as written.
fix: Decide that the agent goal registry is the single goal-identity mechanism for all harnesses, with FLEET_* env kept only as a bonus for new windows. Add register_goal to the StartGoal steps (03c:82-91), covering both new-window and reuse (bind to the pane's harness_session_id). Add the registry to the agent state dir lists (03-workflows.md:51-53, :297-304) and fix 03c:341. Define reuse eligibility: reuse only if the pane cwd is at or under the target workdir, otherwise SESSION_NOT_AVAILABLE; AGENT_ENSURES worktrees therefore need a new window. In REPO_DRIVER mode register by session_id and goal file, never by the shared main-checkout cwd. Release on MERGED/CLEARED/CLOSED and on PruneWorktree. Additive Snapshot.goal_registry[] lets the hub detect loss and rebuild.
verify: Confirmed. 03c-goals.md:87-91 puts FLEET_GOAL_ID/FLEET_PANE_KEY in the env only in ensure_window, which reuse skips (no reuse variant in command_goal.proto:109-123). 01d-goal-hooks.md:40-43 has Claude/Codex hooks gate on that pane env var, and a running harness cannot gain or replace an env var, so a reused pane keeps the previous goal's tag or none. 01d:44-49 says StartGoal writes a Muse worktree-path registry in the agent state dir, but 03c:82-91 has no registry step, 03c:341 says 'Nothing goal-specific on the agent beyond the command log', 03-workflows.md:51-53 and :297-304 omit it from the state dir lists, and nothing releases it or exposes it in snapshot.proto. 01d:263-267 only raises the cd-outside-worktree case, not what cwd a reused session has. ensure_worktree runs before pick_session (03c:82-91), so with AGENT_ENSURES the reused harness sits in another directory; 03-workflows.md:130-131 and 03c:265 (PANE_LOST/orphan detection) key on the same tag. Downgraded from blocker: nothing in the protos blocks implementation, the fix is additive, and without the Stop guard the W6 corrective nudge still covers a stopped goal, so this degrades v2 reuse rather than stopping it. It must be decided before the agent goal registry and hooks are built.
resolution: Same registry design as goal-binding-reused-pane: register_goal covers new-window and reuse, the registry is in the agent state dir lists (03-workflows, 03c), released on ReleaseGoal, pane exit and PruneWorktree, rebuilt from FLEET_GOAL_ID for new windows or by RegisterGoal for reused panes, and REPO_DRIVER registers by pane and session id, never the shared checkout path.

But HarnessConditionKind (harness.proto:199-213) has only PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, USAGE_LIMIT, SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, NETWORK, OTHER; HookEventKind (events.proto:197-204) has no INTERRUPT although Codex and Muse fire Interrupt hooks (01d:31-35, E8 in 01-agent-capabilities.md:~249); GoalLineState (harness.proto:145-155) only mirrors the goal file; hub GoalPhase PAUSED is defined only for operator/review-loop/reserve (goal.proto:36-37, 03c-goals.md:259). title: Agent event seq and hub connection epoch can regress after a crash or restore, silently discarding events or commands
evidence: events.proto:27-28 says seq is 'persisted, never reused'; W2 persists only the ring ('per event, fsync batched <= 1 s', 03-workflows.md:299) and the ring holds only never-dropped/coalesced kinds (03-workflows.md:254-255), so SHED events (pane_summary, resource_sample, heartbeat-adjacent) consume seq numbers that are never persisted. The hub applies later events 'only if seq > last_event_seq' (03-workflows.md:173-175) and keeps hub_last_event_seq per machine (agent.proto:178-179). After an agent crash the counter restarts from the last persisted ring seq and re-emits numbers the hub already saw, which are dropped as duplicates; same after a state-dir wipe or VM revert (install_id changes, seq restarts at 1). On the hub side the epoch is 'epoch+1' of the stored value (03-workflows.md:248); after a store restore (03-workflows.md:325) the hub can issue an epoch the agent already used (Hello.last_epoch=7, last_applied_command_seq=41, agent.proto:154-155), and the agent then rejects the new epoch's seq 1..41 as SEQ_REPLAYED (02-contracts.md envelope checks).
problem: No rule keeps either counter monotonic across crash/restore, and nothing tells the hub that an agent's seq space was reset.
fix: Specify: the agent persists a seq high-water mark in reserved blocks and sets its floor to max(local, HelloAck.hub_last_event_seq) after each HelloAck. The hub sets epoch = max(stored, Hello.last_epoch) + 1 and treats Hello.last_event_seq < hub_last_event_seq as agent rollback (keep history, SnapshotRequest{reason='seq_rollback'}). Add seq high-water mark and install_id to the agent state-dir lists and a row to the W2 failure table.
verify: Confirmed no rule keeps either counter monotonic. events.proto:27 says seq is 'persisted, never reused', but the persisted ring (03-workflows.md:299, 254-255) holds only never-dropped and coalesced kinds. Shed events (02-contracts.md:256-258 table: pane_summary, resource_sample, spool_status) consume seq numbers and are never persisted, so after an agent crash the counter restarts from the last ring seq. The hub applies later events 'only if seq > last_event_seq' (03-workflows.md:173-175) and would drop a restarted agent's events as duplicates until it passes the old number; state-dir wipe or VM revert is the same. A repo-wide grep finds no high-water mark, floor or rollback rule. Epoch is 'epoch+1' (03-workflows.md:248) with no max against Hello.last_epoch (agent.proto:154-155), so a restored hub store can reissue an epoch and trip SEQ_REPLAYED (02-contracts.md:183-184). This is a rules gap with no required proto change.
resolution: 02i "Sequence numbers" and "Connection epoch": agent persists seq_hwm in blocks of 1024, floors seq above HelloAck.hub_last_event_seq, hub treats Hello.last_event_seq below its stored value, a counter decrease or a new install_id as agent rollback (event_generation, marker, audit machine.install_changed), epoch = max(stored, Hello.last_epoch)+1 and the agent refuses a regressed epoch. agent.proto comments; W1/W2 persistence and failure rows; 03f restore.

title: Seq-gap detection cannot tell shedding from loss, and 'replayed seq <= Snapshot.seq is history only' contradicts the W2 failure rows
evidence: 03-workflows.md:260-262 and 02-contracts.md:256-258 say Heartbeat.event_seq lets the hub detect a gap 'caused by ring overflow' and by shedding, then repair it with SnapshotRequest{event_gap}. But gaps in seq are normal: SHED events (pane_summary every 5 s per pane, resource_sample, spool_status) and COALESCE replacements (usage, branch_state, probe_health; 03-workflows.md:254-255 'latest per key wins') delete seq numbers by design, so every hub that sees a hole would request a snapshot, and a real loss of a never-dropped event looks identical. Separately, 03-workflows.md:243/:258-260, 02-contracts.md:217 and 03f-hub-internals.md:60 say replayed events with seq <= Snapshot.seq go to history only, yet 03-workflows.md:328 says the replayed PaneExited lets 'W6 evaluate the one-nudge rule once' and :331 says the replayed AvailabilityChanged{keystroke} drives human_at_keyboard_until 'from the replayed timestamp'; :329-330 say HarnessCondition and Prompt events 'raise and retire in one batch'. History-only means none of that runs.
problem: No wire field distinguishes deliberate drops from lost never-drop events, and the apply rule for replayed never-drop events that feed derived goal/triage flags is contradictory.
fix: Doc fix: state that gap detection compares Heartbeat.event_seq with the hub's highest stored seq, never contiguity. Fix the :331 row once last_input_at exists on TmuxPane (snapshot-derived rather than replay-derived). Optionally add a persisted ring_evicted_never_drop_total to Hello/Heartbeat so the timeline gap marker has a wire source.
verify: Partly confirmed, overstated. Real: 03-workflows.md:331 says a replayed AvailabilityChanged{keystroke} drives human_at_keyboard_until 'from the replayed timestamp', while 03-workflows.md:243/:258-260, 02-contracts.md:217 and 03f-hub-internals.md:60 say replayed events with seq <= Snapshot.seq go to history only; the snapshot carries no input timestamp (see goal-pane-input finding), so that row cannot work as written. Also 02-contracts.md:256-258 says Heartbeat.event_seq makes a gap 'caused by shedding' visible and repairable by SnapshotRequest, without saying whether the hub compares highest-seq (stable) or contiguity (would false-trigger). Overstated: the hub compares Heartbeat.event_seq with its highest stored seq, not hole-by-hole, so shed events do not by themselves force a snapshot per hole. The PaneExited row (:328) is consistent with history-only because the snapshot already shows the pane dead. 03-workflows.md failure table already says 'dropped ring entries counted and gap shown on the timeline', though no wire field carries that count.
resolution: New EventCounters{shed_total, coalesced_total, evicted_total} in Hello.event_counters and Heartbeat.events: only a rise of evicted_total is loss (SnapshotRequest event_lost plus a timeline gap marker); contiguity and Heartbeat.event_seq are never used to infer loss. Replay rule rewritten in 02i, 02-contracts and W2: seq <= Snapshot.seq is history only and runs no rule, with a table of the snapshot field that carries each effect; audit rows stay idempotent.

title: SessionLog hole/duplicate handling has no negative ack, gap_before offset semantics are undefined, and a restored hub wedges streams
evidence: 03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:262 accepts a chunk only at the stored end, 'duplicate (re-ack)', and for a hole 'refuse (ack stays)' (:337 'the agent resends from there'). LogAck (streams.proto:143-155) is only sent on success, so after a refusal the agent receives nothing and cannot learn the hub's stored end. gap_before (streams.proto:124) says 'bytes lost before this chunk' but not whether offset skips them; W9 :321 says 'contiguous except across an explicit gap_before' while the accept rule is 'offset = stored end'. Hub restore from an older backup (or 'truncate trailing partial frame to last indexed offset', :326) leaves the hub end below an agent that already dropped spool <= its older ack (:313 'drop spool <= acked_offset'): every later chunk is a hole, the agent no longer has the bytes to resend, and no rule lets it declare a gap. Also 03d:260 and :277-283 still describe one frame per 10 s / 256 KiB, contradicting the S2 framing in streams.proto:105-112 and 02-contracts.md log framing (one frame up to 5 min/4 MiB, frame_start/frame_raw_offset not in the W9 sequence), and the hub writes '<session>/<stream>/<day>.zst' (:263) without saying a day rollover mid-frame must wait for the next frame_start, which replay-from-frame_raw_offset needs.
problem: Missing: hub reply on refused chunks, precise offset arithmetic across gaps, agent behaviour when the hub is behind the agent's spool floor, file-rotation rule for frames, and W9 text/sequence not updated for the frame model.
fix: Hub answers every chunk with LogAck{key, acked_offset = stored_end}, accepted or refused. On acked_offset below its spool floor the agent sends the next chunk with gap_before = floor - acked_offset, offset = floor, frame_start = true. Accept rule becomes offset == stored_end + gap_before. Hub rotates day files only at a frame_start chunk. Rewrite the W9 sequence and rules to the frame model and add frame_start/frame_raw_offset to the log_segments index columns.
verify: Confirmed. 03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:262 accepts a chunk only at the stored end and for a hole 'refuse (ack stays)' (:337 'the agent resends from there'), but LogAck (streams.proto:143-155) is only specified as a success reply, so a refused chunk gives the agent no way to learn the hub's stored end. gap_before (streams.proto:124) does not say whether offset skips the lost bytes, and the 03d accept rule 'offset = stored end' (:262, :321) conflicts with 'contiguous except across an explicit gap_before'. If the hub is restored from backup or truncates (:326) below an agent that already dropped spool <= acked_offset (:313), every later chunk is a hole and the agent cannot resend or declare a gap. 03d:260 and :277-283 still describe zstd frames per 10 s or 256 KiB, contradicting the frame model in streams.proto:105-112 (one frame up to 5 min or 4 MiB, frame_start, frame_raw_offset); the sequence diagram omits both fields. Day-file rotation (:263) is not tied to frame_start, which replay from frame_raw_offset needs.
resolution: streams.proto: LogAck now answers every chunk with acked_offset = stored end and a new LogAckStatus (STORED, DUPLICATE, HOLE, UNKNOWN_STREAM); gap_before semantics defined (offset = acked end + gap_before, accept rule offset == stored_end + gap_before); an agent whose spool floor is above the hub's end sends gap_before = floor - end with frame_start. 03d W9 rewritten to the frame model (day files rotate only at frame_start; frame_start and frame_raw_offset in log_segments), 03f keys.

title: SetLogCapture cannot give the agent a SessionId, so LogStreamKey.session_id is empty for developer sessions
evidence: command_goal.proto:212-215 SetLogCapture{SessionTarget session, enabled}: the target is by tmux_id/name, no hub SessionId. snapshot.proto:159-160 says TmuxSession.session_id is 'empty for the developer's own'. hub session.proto:71-76 says the hub assigns a SessionId to every observed session bound to (machine, server_start_id, tmux_id), and SetLogCaptureRequest carries it (session.proto:260-264). The agent must still fill LogStreamKey{session_id, pane, stream} on every LogChunk (streams.proto:113-131, harness.proto:231-235), name its spool directory spool/<session>/<stream>/ (03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:313) and the hub names files and log_segments by <session> (03d:263, :315).
problem: For the developer-session capture path the agent has no session id to put in the key, so the hub must guess by PaneKey and the spool, ack and replay keys diverge; an empty key.session_id also collides with LogAck.all_streams semantics.
fix: Either document that for developer sessions the agent leaves key.session_id empty, keys its spool by PaneKey, and the hub fills in the SessionId from key.pane, or add an optional SetLogCapture.session_id so the agent echoes it in every LogChunk.key. Pick one and state it in 02-contracts.md K1 and 03d.
verify: Gap confirmed but severity overstated. SetLogCapture (command_goal.proto:212-215) carries a SessionTarget, whose oneof (command_tmux.proto:22-33) holds session_id, name or tmux_id; for a developer session the agent only knows tmux_id (TmuxSession.session_id is empty for developer sessions, snapshot.proto:159-160), so it has no hub SessionId for LogStreamKey.session_id (streams.proto:113-131) or the spool path (03d:313). However PaneKey (ids.proto:91-101) plus the hub's (machine, server_start_id, tmux_id) binding (session.proto:71-76) lets the hub resolve the SessionId from key.pane deterministically, so this is an unstated convention, not an unsolvable problem. The claimed collision with LogAck.all_streams is unfounded (that uses an explicit bool, streams.proto:153-155).
resolution: harness.proto LogStreamKey: on the agent wire the identity is (pane, stream) and session_id is optional, filled in by the hub from (machine, server_start_id, tmux id); LogAck echoes the key as sent; the spool is keyed by pane. SetLogCapture comment, 02-contracts K1 and 03d W9 "Stream identity".

title: Enroll/Connect-level failures (token reasons, fleet mismatch, unknown machine) have no typed representation
evidence: 03-workflows.md:184 says Enroll 'fails with a gRPC error naming the reason' (expired, used) and the agent prints it, but ReasonCode (status.proto:72-168) has no token/enroll codes; ErrorDetail on a unary RPC error is only defined for the hub API (status.proto:155-185). verify: Mostly speculative; one real piece. title: GoalPhase has no queued/expired/abandoned phase and 'active' is never defined, so the uniqueness constraints and slot accounting cannot be implemented
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:21-54 (19 phases; no READY, EXPIRED, ABANDONED, CANCELLED). docs/specs/03c-goals.md:108-114 state diagram goes STARTING --> READY (EXPIRED) and START_FAILED --> READY, but READY is a WorkStage (api/fleet/hub/v1/work.proto:21), not a GoalPhase. 03c:63-66 + docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md race table: unique '(work_item) WHERE state IN (STARTING, RUNNING, …)' and goals unique '(repo, branch) active' (03f:105) -- the list is literally elided with '…'. docs/design.md:277-283 defines active vs total slots (waiting goals are total-only) but no phase mapping. api/fleet/agent/v1/agent.proto:203-205 Heartbeat.counts.goal_panes_by_state is keyed by GoalLineState names (WORKING, BLOCKED_WATCH) while the hub counts by phase.
problem: (1) Which row does an EXPIRED or START_FAILED start become? The goal row exists (goal_id assigned before send, StartGoalResponse.goal) but the diagram sends it back to a work-item stage. It is undefined whether a retry reuses goal_id or mints a new one; Goal.machine is single-valued and Goal.start_error is 'last failure', yet 'MANUAL_ONLY after 3 failures on different machines' needs per-attempt history, and there is no attempt/previous_goal field. (2) No table says which phases are 'active' for the DB unique indexes, which consume an active slot (quota), which consume only a total slot (WAITING, BLOCKED_OWNER, PAUSED, LIMIT_WAIT, COOLDOWN, VERIFYING, DISAGREE, PANE_LOST, MERGED before CLOSED), and which count toward AccountPacing.active_goals and max_parallel_goals_per_repo. (3) The slot_mismatch rule ('disagrees by more than one', 03c:63-66) compares line-state counts from the agent to phase counts on the hub with no defined mapping; a LIMIT_WAIT or PAUSED goal still has line_state WORKING, so the check will fire spuriously. (4) GOAL_PHASE_MANUAL_ONLY duplicates WORK_STAGE_MANUAL_ONLY with a different meaning (3 failed starts vs untrusted).
fix: Add a normative table in 03c/03f mapping every GoalPhase to ACTIVE_QUOTA / HOLDS_SLOT_ONLY / TERMINAL, used for the unique-active indexes, MachineSlots, AccountPacing.active_goals, repo cap and the heartbeat check (compare only ACTIVE_QUOTA phases to line_state=WORKING). Add GOAL_PHASE_ABANDONED (expired start, operator not-started, superseded). Decide one id rule (each dispatch attempt = new goal_id, add Goal.attempt and Goal.previous_goal) and state that EXPIRED/START_FAILED/CLEARED rows are terminal while the WorkItem stage returns to READY. Rename Goal-side MANUAL_ONLY to START_EXHAUSTED or document it as work-item-only.
verify: Confirmed. 03f-hub-internals.md:56 defines the unique index as `WHERE state IN (STARTING, RUNNING, …)` and 03f:104 / 03c:32,170 say only 'active', so the set is never listed. 03c:105-114 'goal start' diagram sends EXPIRED/START_FAILED/START_UNKNOWN back to `READY`, which is a WorkStage (work.proto:21), not a GoalPhase (goal.proto:21-54, no ABANDONED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED). design.md:277-283 defines active vs total slots with no phase mapping. 03c:67-68 compares agent `goal_panes_by_state` (keyed by GoalLineState names, agent.proto:203-205) to hub phase counts; LIMIT_WAIT/PAUSED goals keep line_state WORKING so the mismatch check is ill-defined. GOAL_PHASE_MANUAL_ONLY (goal.proto:52-53) duplicates WORK_STAGE_MANUAL_ONLY with different meaning. Goal.start_error (goal.proto:~78) is single-valued and there is no attempt/previous_goal, so '3 failures on different machines' (03c:114) has no data. Severity downgraded from blocker: it is a missing spec table plus additive enum values/fields, not a wire-contract break.

title: A person interrupting or pausing a goal at the machine (owner-paused) has no wire event, condition kind, phase or triage kind, and 03c contradicts 01d; PAUSED has no reason
evidence: docs/specs/01d-goal-hooks.md:124-127: 'An interrupt is the developer's decision... agent reports HarnessCondition... hub opens Triage item goal interrupted -- resume?... Nothing resumes automatically.' But api/fleet/type/v1/harness.proto:199-213 HarnessConditionKind has no INTERRUPTED; api/fleet/agent/v1/events.proto:197-204 HookEventKind has no INTERRUPT (01d:60-63 says Codex and Muse have an Interrupt hook); api/fleet/hub/v1/triage.proto:20-40 TriageKind has no interrupted or owner-paused kind although docs/design.md:198 lists an 'owner paused' chip. 03c:284-288 treats ActivityTransition{IDLE} on a WORKING goal as 'stopped without DONE' and 03c:367 suppresses nudges only for 10 min after a keystroke (human_at_keyboard_until), after which 03c:290-296 types 'Your goal is still active. In 03c: INTERRUPTED on a goal pane -> PAUSED{OWNER_AT_MACHINE}, exempt from the corrective nudge, never auto-resumed; RESERVE pauses auto-resume at the deciding bucket resets_at; review-loop cap compares review_rounds minus baseline.
verify: Confirmed. 01d-goal-hooks.md:124-127 says the agent reports a HarnessCondition for an interrupt and the hub opens a 'goal interrupted' triage item, nothing resumes automatically. But HarnessConditionKind (harness.proto:~199-213) has no INTERRUPTED, HookEventKind (events.proto:~197-204) has no INTERRUPT although 01d:34-35 lists the Interrupt hook, and TriageKind (triage.proto:20-40) has no interrupted/paused kind although design.md:198 lists an 'owner paused' chip. 03c:284-289 treats IDLE on a WORKING goal as 'stopped without DONE', suppressed only by human_at_keyboard_until (10 min, 03c:273,367), then 03c:290-296 types the corrective 'Your goal is still active. Continue' nudge, which overrides a deliberate Esc. title: DISAGREE -> RUNNING ('not done') has no working mechanism: the harness goal is already achieved/cleared and the goal file still says DONE

title: Provider-side changes while a goal runs (issue closed or cancelled, change request merged by a human or closed unmerged) have no transition; CANCELLED has no phase; goal end states have no work-item stage mapping
evidence: docs/specs/03c-goals.md:258 and :305 only evaluate provider state after DONE ('Merged or the work item closed -> MERGED'); api/fleet/integration/v1/integration.proto:110-116 WORK_ITEM_STATE_CANCELLED 'Closed without being done... never as success'; api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto has no cancelled/closed-not-done phase; docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md stage diagram (RUNNING --> DONE_CLAIMED only; SEEN --> MANUAL_ONLY has no exit; SEEN --> CLOSED but not RUNNING --> CLOSED); api/fleet/hub/v1/work.proto:18-32 WorkStage.
problem: (1) Issue closed 'not planned' or the PR closed/merged by a human while the goal is RUNNING or WAITING: nothing reacts, so the harness keeps spending quota until DONE or stuck. (2) After DONE, 03c maps 'work item closed' to MERGED, which runs free-the-worker and prune; CANCELLED/CLOSED-without-merge must not be 'MERGED' (integration.proto says it is never success) and no phase can express it. (3) No mapping from goal terminal phases to WorkStage: after CLEARED, STUCK + clear, PANE_LOST timeout or ABANDONED does the item go back to READY (the scheduler then auto-redispatches an item the operator just cleared, 03c:263), CLAIMED_ELSEWHERE or MANUAL_ONLY? (4) WorkStage MANUAL_ONLY has no exit when an allow-listed user later labels the item.
fix: Add GOAL_PHASE_CANCELLED (terminal, frees worker, no success metric) and an external-change rule: on mirror updates for non-terminal goals, external merge -> VERIFYING, external close/cancel -> triage 'work item closed under a running goal' and PAUSED. Add a goal-phase -> WorkItem.stage table (CLEARED/ABANDONED/START_EXHAUSTED -> MANUAL_ONLY until operator requeue, CANCELLED/MERGED -> CLOSED) and MANUAL_ONLY --> READY on trusted-label change or operator requeue.
verify: Confirmed. 03c:228,258,305 evaluate provider state only after DONE, and map 'work item closed' to MERGED (which frees the worker and prunes). integration.proto:110-116 says CANCELLED frees the worker but is 'never as success', yet goal.proto:21-54 has no phase to express it. 03b-usage-and-sync.md:275-287 stage diagram has no RUNNING/DISPATCHED --> CLOSED or READY, and MANUAL_ONLY has no exit edge; nothing maps CLEARED/STUCK+clear/PANE_LOST timeout to a WorkStage, while 03c:8 wakes the scheduler on CLEARED and 03c:263 sends the item back to READY (auto-redispatch of an item the operator just cleared). Nothing reacts to an issue closed or CR merged/closed by a human while the goal is RUNNING/WAITING.

title: Routines have a contract but no workflow: run creation, numbering, trigger evaluation, done-rule inputs and snapshotting are unspecified and some done rules are unverifiable
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/routine.proto:18-77; docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:208-220 is the only behavioural text; grep shows no routine in docs/specs/03*.md (W5 planning rules 03c:53-76 and W6 03c:296-312 never mention ROUTINE or done_rule). api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:63-69 Goal has routine id but no done_rule or report_path. api/fleet/integration/v1/integration.proto:288-299 IntegrationProviderService has no file/path-exists RPC and no CR-by-branch lookup. docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:243-246 finds the CR by BranchState.branch.
problem: (1) DONE_RULE_REPORT_WRITTEN ('report_path exists on the pushed branch', routine.proto:48-49) cannot be checked: the provider interface is read-only list/get of work items and change requests only. (2) DONE_RULE_CHANGE_REQUEST_MERGED for a run has no linked work item (so the 03b fallback on linked_work_items, 03b:269, is empty) and in REPO_DRIVER mode no BranchState branch (see repo-driver-branch-visibility), so the CR cannot be found. (3) The rule and path are read from the Routine at verification time, but UpdateRoutine mid-run or DeleteRoutine ('Running goals continue', routine.proto:128) changes or removes them; the goal must carry a snapshot. (4) Run lifecycle undefined: who allocates '<routine id>/<run number>' and when (before or after preflight succeeds; does a START_FAILED run count in run_count), what happens to the hub-made WorkItem stage/trusted values, whether missed cron fires during a hub outage are skipped (03c:'no catch-up floods' says skipped for backlog but cron is not mentioned), DST in CronTrigger.timezone, and whether min_interval_hours counts from start or finish. (5) 'A run never starts while the previous run's goal is active' means a STUCK or LIMIT_WAIT run blocks the routine for days with no triage. (6) Routine has no model, effort, fresh_context, account or machine constraint although GoalSpec supports them, so a sweep cannot ask for a cheap model. (7) Routine harness unset = 'any harness the scheduler picks' but no selection rule; this is the natural consumer of AccountPacing.projected_unused_percent / idle_while_behind (spend leftover quota) and nothing says so.
fix: Add a W5b 'Routine run' section to 03c (trigger evaluation in the scheduler pass, run-number allocation inside the planning tx, hub-made WorkItem created at DISPATCHED, at most one missed cron fire, blocked-run triage after N hours). Snapshot done_rule and report_path onto the Goal at plan time. Decide REPORT_WRITTEN verification: either an integration PathExists RPC or agent-side git state reported as an event. Add Routine.model, effort, fresh_context, optional account pin; harness-unset routines pick by highest projected_unused_percent.
verify: Confirmed. grep of docs/specs/03*.md and design.md finds no routine workflow (only unrelated 'routine' substrings); the sole behavioural text is 02b-hub-api.md:208-220 and routine.proto:18-77. integration.proto:288-299 has no file/path-exists RPC, so DONE_RULE_REPORT_WRITTEN (routine.proto:48-49) cannot be verified through the provider interface; CHANGE_REQUEST_MERGED for a run has no linked work item and CR lookup keys on BranchState.branch (03b:244), which REPO_DRIVER goals lack (see repo-driver-branch-visibility). Goal (goal.proto:63-69) carries only the routine id, so UpdateRoutine/DeleteRoutine (routine.proto:~128) mid-run changes the done rule. Routine has no model/effort/fresh_context/account fields though GoalSpec does (command_goal.proto:56-65). Run numbering, missed-cron catch-up, blocked-run triage and harness-unset selection are unspecified. Some sub-points (7, DST) are minor.

title: IntegrationProviderService cannot express the queries W4/W6 rely on, and ChangeRequest lacks the fields W6 reads
evidence: api/fleet/integration/v1/integration.proto:249-254 ListChangeRequestsRequest has only repo, updated_after, paging; :263-265 GetChangeRequestRequest takes a ref; :73-75 capability batch_query is declared ('verification of N goals is not N calls') but :291-298 has no batch RPC. docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:213-216 and :243-246 'GraphQL batch: change requests by head_ref... <= 50 per query'. docs/specs/03c-goals.md:308-309 reads ChangeRequest.review_decision and checks.rollup; 03b:208-210 mirror lists head_ref/head_sha/review_decision; integration.proto:152-203 has CheckSummary{passing,failing,pending,skipped}, repeated Review, source_branch, head_commit, and no review_decision or rollup (03g:128 says head_ref=source_branch, head_sha=head_commit was reconciled, review_decision and rollup were not). 03b:208 mirror also says WorkItem.claim (singular) vs integration.proto:141 repeated claims.
problem: (1) A change request cannot be found by branch through the provider-neutral interface; the GitHub GraphQL headRefName trick lives only in prose, so a GitLab/Jira adapter implementing the proto cannot serve the verifier. (2) batch_query is a capability flag with nothing to batch. (3) 'Approved and green' (open question 9, 03g:151-152) is the no-merge-consent completion test, but the proto has no normalized review_decision (branch protection, required reviewers, CODEOWNERS are provider logic) and no checks rollup enum; deriving it from reviews[] in the hub is wrong on GitHub. (4) The hub mirror shape in 03b disagrees with the proto it claims to be.
fix: Add ChangeRequest.review_decision (NONE|REQUIRED|APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUESTED) computed by the adapter and either CheckSummary.rollup or a documented derivation from the counts; fix the 03b:203-208 mirror text to the real proto names; add ListChangeRequestsRequest.source_branches or BatchGetChangeRequests and only advertise batch_query when it exists (or drop the flag).
verify: Confirmed with caveats. integration.proto:249-254 ListChangeRequestsRequest has no source_branch filter, and the service (:288-299) has no batch RPC although batch_query is declared (:73-75). ChangeRequest (:152-203) has no review_decision and CheckSummary (:~165-172) has no rollup, yet 03c:308-309 and open question 9 (03g:151-152) use `review_decision=APPROVED` and `checks.rollup=SUCCESS`; 03b:203-208 mirror text names head_ref, head_sha, review_decision, trusted and a singular claim, which do not exist in the proto (03g:125 reconciled only head_ref/head_sha). Overstated: the hub can find a CR by branch from its own mirror (03f:122 index on head_ref) since ListChangeRequests with updated_after feeds it, and CheckSummary counts let a rollup be derived, so the branch-lookup and batch gaps cost efficiency and provider neutrality rather than blocking implementation. The review_decision gap is real: reviews[] cannot encode required-reviewer/CODEOWNERS rules.

title: The trusted-issues gate cannot be evaluated from the integration contract: label actor is not carried, and the allow-list is a flat string list
evidence: docs/design.md:311-313 'issues opened or labelled agent-ready by an allow-listed user'; docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:241-243 'label agent-ready whose LABELED_EVENT.actor in allowlist (timeline query)'; api/fleet/integration/v1/integration.proto:139 WorkItem.labels is repeated string and Claim.by exists only for claims (:119-128); api/fleet/hub/v1/settings.proto:36-38 HubSettings.trusted_label (one string) and trusted_users (repeated string); api/fleet/hub/v1/work.proto:44-45 WorkItem.trusted bool.
problem: The adapter is read-only and does not know the hub's allow-list, and the provider data it returns has no 'who applied label X, when'. So neither side can compute the gate for the label path. Logins are provider-local (a GitHub 'alice' and a Jira 'alice' are different people), yet trusted_users is one flat list and trusted_label one string for all integrations (Jira uses status or label per 03b:265). There is also no rule for revocation: label removed or edited after dispatch, or trust checked at plan time but the body fetched later (GetWorkItem include_body) -- the safety rail is the one thing standing between untrusted issue text and an agent with push/merge rights.
fix: Have the adapter return label evidence (repeated LabelEvent{name, applied_by Person, applied_at}, capability labels_with_actor) and let the hub compute `trusted` at plan time. Make trusted_users repeated TrustedUser{integration IntegrationId, login} with trusted_label per integration. State in 03b/03c that trust is re-evaluated at plan time from the mirror (updated_at guard) and that a body edit by a non-allow-listed user after the label demotes the item to MANUAL_ONLY.
verify: Confirmed. 03b-usage-and-sync.md:241-243 has the GitHub adapter checking `LABELED_EVENT.actor in allowlist`, but integration.WorkItem.labels is repeated string (integration.proto:139/:~136) with no actor or time, the adapter service is read-only and does not hold the allow-list, and HubSettings.trusted_label/trusted_users (settings.proto:36-38) are flat fleet-wide values; WorkItem.trusted (work.proto:44-45) is a hub bool with no stated computation point. 03b:203-204 claims the integration WorkItem has `trusted`, which it does not. Logins are provider-local, and no rule covers revocation (label removed, body edited after labelling), the main safety rail per design.md:311-313.

title: Per-repo settings referenced by dispatch (consent, parallel cap, worktree mode, branch) have no home in the contract
evidence: docs/specs/03c-goals.md:76 'GoalSpec.consent = repo.consent ∩ account.consent' and :58 per-repo cap; docs/adr/0008-goal-consent-and-account-modes.md:18-33 'repos: - repo: eshu-hq/eshu consent: [...]'; docs/design.md:130 'configurable per repo'; api/fleet/hub/v1/settings.proto:31-45 HubSettings has only fleet-wide default_consent and max_parallel_goals_per_repo; api/fleet/integration/v1/integration.proto:93 and api/fleet/hub/v1/work.proto:157-160 UpdateIntegration edits only label and watched (repeated string); api/fleet/agent/v1/command_goal.proto:46-47 GoalSpec.worktree_mode and branch have no stated hub-side source (grep: WORKTREE_MODE only appears in 03c:36,84-85); api/fleet/hub/v1/common.proto Scope SETTINGS.

title: GoalSpec.model/effort/fresh_context have no composite steps, failure reasons, role path or auto-dispatch defaults; per-model pacing has no input when model is empty
evidence: api/fleet/agent/v1/command_goal.proto:56-65 (model, effort, fresh_context) and api/fleet/agent/v1/command.proto:96-97 CommandProgress.step list; docs/specs/03c-goals.md:84-91 composite steps are preflight, ensure_worktree, pick_session, ensure_window, wait_ready, type_goal, confirm_goal_file only; api/fleet/type/v1/status.proto:68-168 has FRESH_CONTEXT_NOT_ALLOWED but no reason for model or effort unavailable; docs/specs/01b-harness-commands.md:38,44 /model and /effort are SESSION class 'operator role', /clear is DESTRUCTIVE 'local approval or explicit owner action'; status.proto:203-210 Role.SCHEDULER has no documented class permissions (grep: only 02b:154); docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:86-88 pacing uses 'the per-model bucket of the goal's model'; api/fleet/hub/v1/session.proto:41 Pane.model is OpenCode-only.
problem: The typed steps /model, /effort and /clear (and their picker-UI handling, success detection and rollback) are not in the composite, so step_count, retry policy and UNKNOWN_OUTCOME behaviour are undefined for them. Auto-dispatch runs as SCHEDULER; whether that role may type SESSION-class commands, and how a DESTRUCTIVE /clear is approved when nobody is at the machine (AWAITING_LOCAL_CONFIRM would stall a dispatch), is not stated. The planner never says when auto-dispatch sets fresh_context, model or effort (a reused session after MERGED carries the previous goal's context; WorkItem.size S/M/L, work.proto:48-49, is set by no one). When model is empty ('leave as is') the hub cannot know which per-model bucket (weekly_fable) applies, so the exhaustion rule at 03b:86-88 is undefined.
fix: Doc-level: add optional steps set_model, set_effort, clear_context between wait_ready and type_goal with additive reasons MODEL_UNAVAILABLE/EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED; state SCHEDULER may use GOAL and SESSION classes and fresh_context only in fleet-started sessions; rule: auto-dispatch into a reused session sets fresh_context=true; have StartGoalResult echo the effective model so pacing uses the right bucket, or evaluate only weekly_all plus the harness default model's bucket when model is empty.
verify: Confirmed but smaller than claimed. 03c:82-91 composite steps omit set_model/set_effort/clear_context, and status.proto has only REASON_CODE_FRESH_CONTEXT_NOT_ALLOWED (:148), no model/effort reasons. However CommandProgress.step is a free string ('e.g.', command.proto:~93) so adding steps is non-breaking, and 02-contracts.md:350-360 plus command_goal.proto:56-65 already limit /clear to fleet-started sessions, which answers the DESTRUCTIVE-approval concern (no local confirm is involved). Genuine gaps: SCHEDULER role's allowed classes are undocumented (status.proto:209), planner never says when auto-dispatch sets fresh_context/model/effort, and with empty model the per-model bucket in 03b:86-88 is undefined (Pane.model is OpenCode-only, session.proto:~37).
resolution: Steps set_model, set_effort and clear_context added with MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE and EFFORT_NOT_SUPPORTED; the scheduler may run them inside StartGoal with local approval asked once before step 1 (02g, 02h); auto-dispatch into a reused pane sets fresh_context; StartGoalResult.model and effort let pacing use the right bucket, with weekly_all plus the default model's bucket until then.

title: Session reuse contradicts agent-ensured worktrees (harness cwd cannot change), the hub cannot see a pane's workdir, and prune is ordered before KillWindow
evidence: docs/specs/03c-goals.md:84-91 ensure_worktree runs before pick_session; :86-87 reuse of an available session; :233 and :311-316 'PruneWorktree, KillWindow'; api/fleet/agent/v1/snapshot.proto:111-130 TmuxPane has no cwd/workdir/repo; docs/specs/01d-goal-hooks.md:56-59 Muse goal registry keys on the worktree path a StartGoal records and a cwd at or under it; api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:141-145 GoalPlacement.reuse_session; docs/specs/01-agent-capabilities.md:293-304 (E11 reuse).
problem: A harness process is started in one directory. If the agent creates a fresh worktree for the next goal (AGENT_ENSURES) and then reuses the idle session, the harness is still in the old worktree/branch, the registry path for Muse hooks is wrong, the goal file lands elsewhere, and the new branch is not the one being worked. Reuse is only coherent when the session sits in the repo checkout and the repo's driver (REPO_DRIVER) makes worktrees, or the session was started in the target worktree. The planner (03c:67-71) cannot filter reusable sessions by repo, directory or profile because TmuxPane exposes none of them, so it reserves a session blind and relies on SESSION_NOT_AVAILABLE. Separately, the diagram prunes the worktree before killing the window, removing the directory under a live harness; and the reused-session path leaves the old worktree unpruned forever ('A session that was reused is left alone').
fix: Add TmuxPane.workdir (Workdir{repo, relative_path}) derived by the agent. Rule in 03c: reuse is eligible only when pane.workdir.repo == goal repo and (worktree_mode == REPO_DRIVER, or the session was started in the target worktree); otherwise always ensure_window. Order cleanup KillWindow then PruneWorktree and prune the previous goal's agent-created worktree when its session is reused.
verify: Confirmed. TmuxPane (snapshot.proto:111-130) and hub Pane (session.proto:19-40) carry no workdir/repo, so the planner (03c:67-71) cannot filter reusable sessions by repo and relies on SESSION_NOT_AVAILABLE. 03c:84-91 runs ensure_worktree (AGENT_ENSURES) before pick_session, and a reused harness process keeps its original cwd, so reuse in AGENT_ENSURES mode lands the goal in the old worktree/branch (also breaking the Muse registry path in 01d:56-59). 03c:233 and :311-316 list PruneWorktree before KillWindow, and :316 'A session that was reused is left alone' leaves the previous worktree unpruned.
resolution: A reused pane keeps its directory: no ensure_worktree, the goal starts a new branch in place (prepare_branch); the planner filters by TmuxPane.workdir.repo. Cleanup is KillWindow then PruneWorktree, with new REASON_CODE_WORKTREE_IN_USE for a worktree a live pane works in (02h, 03c).

title: For REPO_DRIVER goals (eshu, the primary repo) the hub never learns the branch or worktree, breaking CR lookup by head_ref and the one-agent-per-branch rule
evidence: api/fleet/agent/v1/snapshot.proto:194-215 GoalState has goal_file ('relative to the worktree') but no branch, workdir or worktree path; :218-232 BranchState.goal_id and :241-251 RepoCheckout.goal_id are 'set when the worktree was created by fleet' (agent/v1/snapshot.proto RepoCheckout comment); docs/specs/03c-goals.md:84-85 'eshu's driver creates its own, so REPO_DRIVER starts in the main checkout'; docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:243-246 CR lookup uses BranchState.branch; docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md goals unique (repo, branch); docs/design.md:279 'One agent per PR branch'; api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:92 Goal.branch has no stated source.
problem: With a driver-created worktree no BranchState carries goal_id, so Goal.branch stays empty, the head_ref GraphQL batch cannot target the goal's CR, and unique (repo, branch) cannot be enforced. The fallback (03b:269 linked_work_items on any CR updated since dispatch) works for issue goals but not for routines or change-request take-overs, and it is slow (60 s poll) with false matches when two issues are in flight. The Muse registry (01d) and PruneWorktree ('agent-created worktrees only') have the same blind spot.
fix: Add GoalState.workdir and GoalState.branch, filled by the agent from the goal file's directory (git rev-parse) and re-sent on change; set BranchState.goal_id whenever a fleet goal file lives in the worktree regardless of creator; hub maps it to Goal.branch and the CR sync keys on it. Document that PruneWorktree never touches a driver-created worktree.
verify: Confirmed. GoalState (snapshot.proto:194-215) has goal_file relative to the worktree but no branch/workdir; RepoCheckout.goal_id is 'set when the worktree was created by fleet' (snapshot.proto:~236), and 03c:84-85 says REPO_DRIVER starts in the main checkout with the driver creating its own worktree, so no BranchState is tied to the goal. 03b:243-246 finds the CR via BranchState.branch, 03f:104 requires unique (repo, branch), design.md:279 requires one agent per branch, yet Goal.branch (goal.proto:33) has no documented source (ui-contract-map.md:109 only reads it). The 03b:269 linked_work_items fallback covers issue goals but not routines or CR take-overs. Affects eshu, the primary repo.
resolution: GoalState gains worktree_path and branch (from the goal file's directory, re-sent on change) so Goal.status.branch, head_ref lookup and the one-agent-per-branch rule work for REPO_DRIVER goals; BranchState.goal_id is set whenever a fleet goal file lives in the worktree; PruneWorktree never touches a driver-created worktree (02h).

title: Goal cannot render several states and histories W6 persists or the UI requires
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:57-107 Goal has nudges, no_progress_runs, review_rounds, cooldown_until but no stuck/phase reason, verify_deadline, block owner/action, restarts, usage consumed or transcript path; docs/specs/03c-goals.md:270-275 flags (prompt_pending, human_at_keyboard_until, block_epoch), :246 STUCK reasons session_closed, LOCAL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT, PANE_LOST 10 min, :351-356 goal_transitions and goal_runs ('usage consumed, transcript path'); docs/design.md:204 Session view shows 'run history per goal (restarts, nudges, usage consumed, transcript path)'; docs/specs/ui-contract-map.md goal progress 'not in the contract'; agent GoalState.owner/action (snapshot.proto:206-210) reach the hub only as TriageItem.note free text (triage.proto:109-110); no RPC lists goal_transitions.

verify: Absence confirmed (goal.proto:57-107 has no phase_reason, blocked owner/action, verify_deadline, restarts, usage, transcript path; no ListGoalTransitions RPC), but largely deliberate: ui-contract-map.md:112 records 'goal progress: not in the contract (mock only)', transcripts are v3 (03g/design), and the timeline row (ui-contract-map.md:168) uses ListGoals. title: Start-failure handling table is incomplete and contradicts the agent contract on DISK_LOW and version support; drain interplay with outbox and respawn is unspecified
