title: Telemetry and log counters inside versioned Watch resources (Machine, Session) contradict the version/dedupe rule and the load model
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/machine.proto:115 last_seen_time, :40-41 on_battery/battery, :149-152 load1, mem_available_bytes, clock_skew sit in Machine beside inventories (harnesses[].catalog.entries :137, repos[] :139). api/fleet/hub/v1/session.proto:27-28 Pane.activity/last_output_time and :58-66,89 Session.logs[] SessionLogInfo{raw_bytes, stored_bytes, last_time} change per log chunk. docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:84-90 says version bumps on every committed change and clients drop a change whose (id, version) they already hold; :137-141 says every topic except PANE_SUMMARIES and FLEET_SUMMARY is never dropped (a slow client gets RESYNC_REQUIRED). docs/specs/03g-load-and-handoff.md:30 (row 3) says heartbeats reach browsers only coalesced into the summary strip; :32 (row 5) says summaries are latest-wins; row 12 has 30 log chunks/s and row 6 has 5 activity transitions/s at A50.
problem: If these fields bump `version`, every heartbeat (3.3/s at A50), every log chunk (30/s at A50) and every activity flip re-sends the whole Machine or Session (catalogs, repos, windows, panes) on a never-dropped topic. That is about 100x the fan-out 03g budgets and makes RESYNC_REQUIRED routine. If they do not bump `version`, the 02b (id, version) dedupe makes clients discard the fresh values. 02b has no rule for volatile fields, so each implementer will pick one and the UI will break against the other.
fix: Decide before code and write it in 02b. Option A (clean): move last_seen_time, load1, mem_available_bytes, on_battery, battery, clock_skew into a separate MachineStatus message on a coalesced topic (<=1 per 5-30 s, latest-wins, like FLEET_SUMMARY). Move SessionLogInfo counters to Get-only or a coalesced topic, and drop Pane.last_output_time because PaneSummary carries it. Option B (smaller): keep the fields in Machine/Session, but state that volatile fields are re-sent at most once per N seconds and that the (id, version) dedupe applies to the version, so a throttled bump is expected. Either way add the rule to 02b Versions and ETags. Adding new messages and topics is additive.
verify: Confirmed. machine.proto:115 last_seen_time, :147-152 on_battery/battery/load1/mem_available_bytes/clock_skew sit in Machine beside inventories. common.proto:5 says version is 'bumped on every change'. 02b-hub-api.md:84-90 says version bumps on every committed change and clients drop (id, version) they already hold. 02b:137-141 says every topic except PANE_SUMMARIES and FLEET_SUMMARY is never dropped. ui-contract-map.md:152 uses Machine.last_seen_time on the Machine card, so there is no other path to the value. 03g row 3 says heartbeats reach browsers only coalesced into the summary strip; row 4 puts resource samples on the Machines view. Nothing defines a volatile-field rule. session.proto:58-66 SessionLogInfo counters and Pane.last_output_time/activity (:27-28) have the same ambiguity. The 100x figure is not computed anywhere, but the either/or contradiction is real.
resolution: MachineTelemetry (status), Session status counters and pane activity, Goal first_line and head_commit are marked volatile and coalesced to one Watch message per 30 s or 5 s (02c table); Pane.last_output_time dropped because PaneSummary carries it.

title: LogStreamKey requires a hub-assigned SessionId the agent cannot know for developer sessions
evidence: api/fleet/type/v1/harness.proto:231-235 LogStreamKey{session_id, pane, stream} is the key of every LogChunk (api/fleet/agent/v1/streams.proto:131 key = 12) and LogAck (:151). api/fleet/agent/v1/snapshot.proto:159-160 TmuxSession.session_id is `empty for the developer's own`. api/fleet/hub/v1/session.proto:68-72 says the hub assigns a SessionId to developer sessions, bound to (machine, server_start_id, tmux_id). api/fleet/agent/v1/command_goal.proto:212-215 SetLogCapture addresses the session by SessionTarget, whose `by` is a oneof of session_id OR name OR tmux_id (command_tmux.proto:22-35), so one command cannot carry both the tmux id and the hub SessionId. docs/specs/02-contracts.md:152,263 and 03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:274-286 define the stream as `LogStreamKey{session_id, pane, stream}` and say LogAck must name exactly the chunk's stream.
problem: K1 lets the owner turn on capture for a developer's own session, but the agent has no value to put in LogStreamKey.session_id and no message through which the hub tells it one. The hub's log index (03f-hub-internals.md:110, `log_segments(session_id, stream, raw_offset)`) is keyed by that session id. Either the agent sends an empty session_id and the hub invents the mapping silently, or there is a missing assignment message.
fix: Simplest option is A. PaneKey (server, server_start_id, pane_id) is already unique per machine, and the hub knows the machine from the certificate. So the agent-wire stream identity is (pane, stream), and LogStreamKey.session_id is optional on agent->hub (agent sets it only when it has FLEET_SESSION_ID). The hub resolves the pane to a SessionId on ingest, and LogAck echoes the key as sent. Document this in the LogStreamKey comment and in 02-contracts.md K1.
verify: Confirmed. harness.proto:231-235 LogStreamKey{session_id, pane, stream}. snapshot.proto:159-160 TmuxSession.session_id is empty for the developer's own. session.proto:68-72 has the hub assign a SessionId bound to (machine, server_start_id, tmux_id). command_goal.proto:212-215 SetLogCapture carries a SessionTarget oneof (session_id OR tmux_id), so the hub cannot hand the agent its assigned id there. No other hub-to-agent message carries the assignment. 03d:261 and 02-contracts.md:152 still show session_id in the key.
resolution: Same change as dev-session-log-key (option A): LogStreamKey.session_id is optional on the agent wire, the hub resolves the pane to its SessionId on ingest; documented in harness.proto, 02-contracts K1 and 03d.

title: No hub API to find ended sessions, read the archived last pane summary, or delete a session's logs
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/session.proto:72-92 Session has no lifecycle (no state/end_time); service.proto:58-61 ListSessions only; ReadSessionLogRequest (terminal.proto:97-107) needs a LogStreamKey the caller must already know. Owner decision: ADR 0015:46-48 and 04-technology-review.md:29,158-162 move the last pane summary of each pane to logs.db at session end. docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:29 lists PaneSummary as `Watch only`. ADR 0010:44-45,57-58 and 03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:288 require per-session delete as one audited action and `fleet logs export <session>`; service.proto has no DeleteSessionLog/ExportSessionLog RPC. 03f-hub-internals.md:110 keeps log_sessions `until pruned by size cap`, while sessions rows are permanent only for fleet-created ones (03f:95 area, 03d:192-195).
problem: Logs and archived summaries outlive the session, but a closed developer session leaves no Session resource to find them through. The archived summary has no read path at all. The audited delete that ADR 0010 requires for sensitive logs has no RPC. `fleet logs export` has nothing to call.

Add ListSessionLogs or let an ended Session carry logs[] plus last_summary per pane. Add DeleteSessionLog [ADMIN] with expected_version, audited. ADR 0015:46-48 archives the last pane summary at session end with no read path (02b:29 lists PaneSummary as Watch only). ADR 0010:42,45 and ADR 0015:49 require 'fleet logs export' and per-session audited delete, but no DeleteSessionLog or export RPC exists. 03f:94 keeps only fleet-created sessions permanent, while logs outlive them (03f:110).

title: List/Watch filter fields named in request comments are not fields of the resource, and the grammar is undefined
evidence: docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:52-57 says AIP-160 subset on `the fields named in each request's comment`. Mismatches: api/fleet/hub/v1/session.proto:109-110 ListSessionsRequest filters `harness, available_for_work, goal` but Session (:72-92) has none of them (they live on panes[]); machine.proto:156 filters `label, harness` but fields are `labels`, `harnesses[].harness`; work.proto:91-92 filters `integration, repo, kind, label` but WorkItem has id.integration, item.repos, item.labels; work.proto:119 filters `owned` which exists nowhere; device.proto:92 filters `revoked` but the field is revoked_time. watch.proto:69-72 applies one filter to every topic and says missing fields do not filter. Nothing defines enum literals (`phase = RUNNING` vs GOAL_PHASE_RUNNING), timestamp literals, `in` list syntax, how an id wrapper (MachineId{value}) compares to `machine = "m-12"`, or order_by field names.
problem: The filter vocabulary is a second, undocumented namespace. The hub needs a hand-written parser per field, the TypeScript UI cannot be typed against it, and a later alignment with real field paths would break stored queries and the Watch resume-token filter hash (02b:129-130).
fix: Doc and comment only. Add a per-resource table to 02b (filter name, resource path, type, operators, literal syntax, order_by names). State that enums are written by short name, timestamps are RFC 3339, and id wrappers compare by .value. Mark derived names (pane-level harness, owned) as such, or rename the comments to real resource paths.
verify: Confirmed. 02b:52-55 says AIP-160 subset 'on the fields named in each request's comment'. The mismatches exist. ListSessionsRequest (session.proto:109) names harness, available_for_work and goal, which are Pane fields, not Session fields. ListMachinesRequest (machine.proto:156) names label and harness, but the fields are labels and harnesses[].harness. ListWorkItemsRequest (work.proto:91) names integration, repo, kind, label, which live inside id and item. ListChangeRequestsRequest (work.proto:119) names owned, which exists nowhere (the field is goal). ListDevicesRequest (device.proto:92) names revoked, but the field is revoked_time. Nothing defines enum literals, timestamp literals, id-wrapper comparison or order_by names (grep of 02-contracts and ui-contract-map finds nothing).
resolution: 02c defines the grammar (operators, precedence, literals: enums by short name, RFC 3339 timestamps, id wrappers by value, limits) and a catalogue of filter and order_by names per resource with the resource path and derived (D) fields; List request comments now point to it.

title: Hub-side dispatch refusals have no ReasonCode, so PreflightGoalResponse.hub_checks cannot say why
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:187-193 PreflightGoalResponse.hub_checks is `repeated ErrorDetail` for `SLOTS_FULL, pacing`. ErrorDetail.reason is the closed enum ReasonCode (api/fleet/type/v1/status.proto:72-168); its hub range 500-505 (:155-167) holds only VERSION_MISMATCH, REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT, SCOPE_MISSING, APPROVAL_CLOSED, PAIRING_CODE_MISMATCH, DEVICE_NOT_ACTIVE. docs/specs/03c-goals.md:62-78 (planning rules) refuses for pacing states (RESERVE, SHORT_LIMIT, UNKNOWN, STALE, EXCLUDED, interactive-only accounts), untrusted or claimed work item, integration lag > max_sync_lag, repo cap, consent, no fit machine; 03c:176-178 names them only as metric labels (no_account_capacity, pacing_ahead, no_fit_machine, sync_stale, repo_cap). ui-contract-map.md:78 and :82 render these reasons in the Work dispatch panel.

There is no ReasonCode for untrusted or claimed work item, repo cap, no fit machine, sync lag or empty consent (03c:62-78 refuses on these; 03c:177 only names metric labels). However, account-level refusals are already machine-readable through Account.pacing.state (PacingState incl. RESERVE, SHORT_LIMIT, UNKNOWN, STALE, EXCLUDED, account.proto:28-38), and ui-contract-map.md:75,145 renders 'manual only' from pacing.state = EXCLUDED, not from a ReasonCode. title: Consent acts are `repeated string` in six messages although they are a closed set typed into the harness
evidence: api/fleet/agent/v1/command_goal.proto:40-43 GoalSpec.consent; api/fleet/hub/v1/goal.proto:77 and :157-158; hub/account.proto:113-114; hub/routine.proto:68-69; hub/settings.proto:35 HubSettings.default_consent. ADR 0008:25-34 defines the set push, pr-open, merge. docs/specs/03c-goals.md (Consent form) shows the adapter typing `/goal consent push,pr-open,merge -- <goal_text>` or `(consent: push, pr-open, merge)` into the harness. 02-contracts.md:393-396 states `No shell strings` and typed commands only.
problem: Free strings from the hub are joined into a line typed into a harness. A value containing `--`, a comma or a newline changes what the goal says or ends the consent list early. A typo such as `merge ` silently grants nothing or something else, and the set intersection (repo ∩ account ∩ routine) compares strings. Changing string to enum later alters the JSON form (`push` becomes `CONSENT_ACT_PUSH`) in every hub resource and request, so it is breaking.
fix: Add enum ConsentAct {UNSPECIFIED, PUSH, PR_OPEN, MERGE} to fleet.type.v1 and use repeated ConsentAct in all six places. The agent adapter renders the lowercase hyphenated text itself, and new acts are additive enum values plus an agent capability. If the owner keeps strings, document the allow-list and make the agent reject anything else with INVALID_ARGUMENT.
verify: Confirmed. consent is repeated string in command_goal.proto:43, hub/goal.proto:77 and :158, hub/account.proto:114, hub/routine.proto:69 and hub/settings.proto:35. ADR 0008:25-34 defines the set push, pr-open, merge. 03c:95-99 shows the adapter typing the list into the harness, joined with commas around '--'. command_goal.proto:40 documents the allowed values only in a comment. The string-to-enum change later would alter JSON values in every hub resource, so it is breaking under WIRE_JSON, while doing it now is free.
resolution: New type/v1/consent.proto enum ConsentAct {PUSH, PR_OPEN, MERGE}; used by GoalSpec (agent), GoalDefinition, StartGoalRequest, AccountSpec, RoutineSpec and HubSettings.default_consent; the adapter renders the words itself (03c, 02-contracts).

title: WorkItemRef mixes identity with display fields and is used as the Watch/dedupe id
evidence: api/fleet/type/v1/work.proto:55-75 WorkItemRef{integration, provider, kind, project, key, url, display, provider_name}. api/fleet/hub/v1/work.proto:36,55 use it as WorkItem.id and ChangeRequest.id; GetWorkItemRequest.id (:108) and Goal.work_item/change_request (hub/goal.proto:64,66) take it as input. docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md:99-101 keys the mirror rows by (integration_id, kind, project, key) for work items but (integration_id, repo RepoRef, key) for change_requests. docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:90 dedupes Watch changes by (id, version) and :215-216 builds routine run refs with provider_name "fleet", no integration, key "<routine id>/<run>".
problem: Nothing says which fields are the identity. `url`, `display` and the `provider` hint are mutable or derived. A client comparing ids as whole messages (Map keys, dedupe) will see the same item as different after a title-derived display change. A caller of GetWorkItem does not know which fields to fill. The change_request key in 03f differs from the proto id shape. Routine runs rely on provider_name where integration is empty.
fix: Add a comment on WorkItemRef and a line in 02b: identity = (integration, kind, project, key), with provider_name authoritative only when integration is empty. Hub APIs ignore url, display and provider on input and fill them on output. Align the change_requests key in 03f:100 with this.
verify: Partly mitigated but still a gap. work.proto:55-59 says 'kind is part of the identity', but it never states the full identity tuple, and WorkItemRef also carries mutable or derived url, display and provider (:61-75). hub/work.proto:36,55 use it as the Watch id. 03f:99-101 keys work items by (integration_id, kind, project, key) and change_requests by (integration_id, repo, key), which differs. 02b:215-216 relies on provider_name for routine runs. A comment-level fix is enough; no new message is needed.
resolution: type/v1/work.proto: WorkItemKey{integration, kind, project, key, provider_name} is the identity (id of WorkItem and ChangeRequest, input of Get and StartGoal/PreflightGoal); WorkItemRef is key plus derived url, display, provider. 02b states the rule and 03f keys change_requests the same way.

title: Browser terminal attach has no error channel, auth or framing spec, and ADR 0016 names the wrong messages
evidence: api/fleet/hub/v1/terminal.proto:79-83 AttachClosed{string reason} (free strings "idle_timeout", "session_ended", "agent_offline", "detached") is the only failure signal in AttachTerminalResponse (:86-94); agent-side TermClosed (agent/v1/streams.proto:59-63) uses a different string set ("hub_closed", "agent_shutdown"). terminal.proto:3-6 and docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:226-229 say the browser sends the same messages over a WebSocket. docs/adr/0016-browser-transport.md:34 says the WebSocket carries `TermUp`/`TermDown`, which are agent.v1 types; docs/specs/02b-hub-api.md:17-21 and ADR 0018:46-50 forbid hub messages embedding agent wire types.
problem: Over HTTP/2 a failed attach (PERMISSION_DENIED, REASON_CODE_SESSION_NOT_FOUND, machine offline, ROLE_INSUFFICIENT) arrives as a Connect error with ErrorDetail. Over WebSocket there are no trailers, so the browser gets only a free-text reason and no ErrorDetail, and the UI path (the primary attach path) is less informed than the CLI. The endpoint path, subprotocol, how auth is presented (browsers cannot set Authorization on a WebSocket; device auth is still open), the first-frame rule, frame-to-close-code mapping and AttachAck cadence appear in no spec, and the generated TS client cannot cover it. ADR 0016's wire names contradict the hub API.
fix: Add an ErrorDetail error field and an AttachCloseReason enum to AttachClosed (keep the string message). Write a short 'Terminal over WebSocket' section in 02b: path, subprotocol, how a browser authenticates (cookie or first-frame token), binary protobuf frames, first frame must be AttachOpen, close-code mapping, and the ack high-water mark. Fix ADR 0016:34 to AttachTerminalRequest/AttachTerminalResponse.
verify: Confirmed. terminal.proto:79-83 AttachClosed has only a free-text reason ('idle_timeout', 'session_ended', 'agent_offline', 'detached') and no ErrorDetail. terminal.proto:1-6 and 02b:226-229 say the browser sends the same messages over a WebSocket. 02b has no WebSocket section: no URL, subprotocol, auth, first-frame rule or close-code mapping, and open question 3 only covers device auth. ADR 0016:34 says the WebSocket carries TermUp/TermDown, which are agent.v1 types (streams.proto:40), contradicting 02b:17-21. The 256 KiB high-water mark is still 'proposed' (terminal.proto:64).
resolution: AttachClosed already carried reason and ErrorDetail (theme A); 02f now specifies endpoint, subprotocol fleet.attach.v1, ticket as first-frame field (AttachOpen.ticket), Host and Origin checks, binary framing and size limits, ack cadence (32 KiB or 200 ms, 256 KiB high-water), close-code mapping per reason. ADR 0016's TermUp/TermDown wording is corrected in ADR 0019 addendum 13 (accepted ADRs are not rewritten).

title: Triage kinds and goal state named in 03c/03d/03e do not exist in the hub enums

title: Specs still describe superseded designs (log files, owner strings, SUPPORTED-only dispatch, goal.stop)
evidence: docs/specs/03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:257-346 (W9 diagram `hub files`, `<session>/<stream>/<day>.zst`, `log_segments`, Persistence table row `Log files: one per (session, stream, day)`) and 03f-hub-internals.md:63,110 contradict ADR 0015:23-36 (chunks as rows in logs.db, one transaction per batch). 03d:146-147,192 still show `owner` on EnsureSession/sessions although agent/v1/command_tmux.proto:76-78 reserves `owner` (now owner_principal). 03c-goals.md:63-64 requires `version_support = SUPPORTED` for dispatch, but ADR 0018:91-98, 02-contracts.md:350-354, 03b-usage-and-sync.md:46 and 03e:210-213 let UNVERIFIED_PARSING dispatch while usage and ready parse live. 02-contracts.md:297 lists capability `goal.stop` although StopGoal was removed (:469-473, command.proto:42-48). title: Enrollment trusts whatever CA the server presents (TOFU), and a lost Enroll response strands the agent
evidence: agent/v1/agent.proto:23-26 (Enroll over server-authenticated TLS with only a token) and :46-48,:71-73 (token sent in EnrollRequest; EnrollResponse supplies the CA chain and `ca_fingerprint` the agent then pins). hub/v1/machine.proto:239-248 (`ca_fingerprint` is 'for the owner to compare'; `enroll_command` is `fleet-agent enroll --hub … --token …` with no fingerprint). docs/specs/01-agent-capabilities.md:117-119 (`fleet-agent enroll --token T [--hub addr]`); docs/adr/0004-agent-connectivity.md:76-81 (fingerprint compared by the owner after the fact); docs/specs/03-workflows.md:120-121 (the impostor defence only applies once the CA is pinned). docs/specs/03-workflows.md:99-106,184-190: the token is burned and the machine row created in one tx; the failure table has no row for a lost response.

The agent must verify the server chain against it before sending the token or CSR. `EnrollResponse.ca_fingerprint` then becomes a self-check. Define Enroll replay: the same (token hash, install_id, CSR public key) within the TTL returns the same certificate and machine_id. Document both in 02-contracts A1. No proto field is strictly required (`enroll_command` string content and CLI flags); additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)

title: Machine deletion and revocation have no state, cascade or live-connection behaviour
evidence: hub/v1/machine.proto:217-226 (DeleteMachine 'revokes the certificate serials; the next Hello is refused', empty response); hub/v1/service.proto:51; MachineState hub/v1/machine.proto:21-30 has no REVOKED/DELETED, though docs/specs/03-workflows.md:154-156 names DELETED. agent/v1/agent.proto:55-58,274-275 (re-enroll with previous_machine_id so history carries over; BYE_REASON_REVOKED). docs/specs/03f-hub-internals.md:87 ('permanent until deleted'). hub/v1/device.proto:80 contrasts: RevokeDevice 'takes effect at once, including open Watch streams'.

title: An older agent silently ignores new tighten-only settings, and probe-interval merge and precedence are undefined
evidence: type/v1/settings.proto:46-73 (SettingValues grows by adding fields; 'unset = no opinion'); agent/v1/agent.proto:232-256 (Settings and SettingsAck.effective, capped_fields only for the local ceiling); docs/specs/02-contracts.md:299 (one capability `settings`, no per-field versioning); docs/specs/02-contracts.md:283-287 (hub supports agents one minor version behind); docs/specs/03e-settings-and-drift.md:36-50 (merge rules list does not include `probe_interval` or `merged_grace`). Probe interval has three carriers: type/v1/settings.proto:69-70, agent/v1/agent.proto:243-245 (`probe_interval_by_account`, 'tighten-only'), agent/v1/command_tmux.proto:48 (EnsureProbe.interval).
problem: A hub upgraded first can send a safety setting (for example a new limit or `block_on_battery`-style flag) that an older agent drops as an unknown field. The ack's `effective` simply omits it, which the UI cannot tell apart from 'no opinion', so the owner believes it is enforced. For probe intervals, 'tighter' is ambiguous (a local floor on frequency is a max, not min(hub, local)) and which of the three channels wins on conflict is unstated. `merged_grace` is hub-only but is delivered to agents.
fix: Add `SettingsAck.unrecognized_fields` (or a `settings_schema` integer in Hello/SettingsAck) so the hub can mark 'not enforced on this agent'. Alternatively advertise `settings.<field>` capabilities. Write the probe-interval merge rule (local value is a minimum interval) and a precedence order (Settings.probe_interval_by_account, then SettingValues.probe_interval, with EnsureProbe.interval only run_now or initial). Remove hub-only fields from agent delivery or mark them echo-only. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: SettingsAck.unrecognized_value_fields and unrecognized_settings_fields (field numbers) let the hub show "not enforced on this machine" (hub Machine.status.unenforced_settings) and keep the machine out of auto-dispatch for a safety limit. Probe interval: precedence by-account > SettingValues.probe_interval > EnsureProbe.interval (initial only), effective = max(hub, local minimum), reported in EffectiveSettings.probe_interval_by_account; merged_grace marked hub-only echo. 03e, settings protos.

title: How the agent derives RepoRef from a checkout (remote choice, forks, multiple checkouts, code_host) is unspecified
evidence: agent/v1/snapshot.proto:232-246 (RepoCheckout has a single `repo`, no remote name or url); docs/specs/01-agent-capabilities.md:368-370 (H1: 'repo reference' only); type/v1/work.proto:12-25 (RepoRef.code_host is a hub-assigned IntegrationId inside a type the agent also fills and receives in Workdir); agent/v1/command_goal.proto:140-150 (EnsureWorktree addresses 'the main checkout'). grep for remote/origin/fork in docs: only ADR 0012:36 'SSH and HTTPS remotes normalize'.
problem: A checkout with `origin` = fork and `upstream` = the watched repo, a checkout with no remote, a repo moved or renamed on the host, or two checkouts of the same repo on one machine all have no defined result. Push-access and ForgeCliStatus.access are per repo, so picking the wrong remote produces false PUSH_ACCESS_MISSING or the wrong work item to repo match. The agent cannot know `code_host` ids, so proto equality of RepoRef across agent and hub will differ unless code_host is excluded from identity.
fix: Specify in 01/02: the remote used (default `origin`, overridable by a local policy setting), reporting of all remotes (or a `remote_name` plus normalized url on RepoCheckout), the rule for duplicate checkouts (prefer the allowed root listed first or the one named in Workdir), and that RepoRef identity is (host, path) only with `code_host` hub-filled and ignored for equality. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: 02h, Repo identity: remote is origin unless local policy names another, RepoCheckout.remote_name and remotes[] (GitRemote, no URLs) report all remotes and the fork case, normalization rules, duplicate checkout choice, and RepoRef identity is (host, path) only with code_host hub-filled and ignored for equality (comment on RepoRef).

title: Agent-clock timestamps drive ordering and waits with only a 5-minute warning for skew
evidence: agent/v1/events.proto:28-30 (`Event.at` agent clock), agent/v1/usage.proto:28-29 (`UsageReading.read_at`), agent/v1/screen.proto:61-64 (resets_at resolved by the agent); hub/v1/machine.proto:151-152 (clock_skew, warning above 5 min); docs/specs/03b-usage-and-sync.md:57,143-144,167 (newest `read_at` wins across machines; ordered by read_at); docs/specs/02-contracts.md:195-197 says skew is measured from `Heartbeat.sent_at` while docs/specs/03-workflows.md:192 says `Hello.sent_at`.
problem: On probe failover two machines read the same account. Newest `read_at` wins, so a machine whose clock is a few minutes fast makes an older reading look current, and `reading_stale` (read_at vs previous reset) is skew-sensitive. A badly wrong or future `Event.at` is stored with no clamp. The contract never says the hub records its own receive time, and the skew source is inconsistent between docs.
fix: State in 02-contracts: the hub stores `received_at` for every event and reading, orders cross-machine data by hub-adjusted time (`at - machine.clock_skew`) or received_at, clamps `at` beyond now plus skew to received_at, and uses one skew source (Hello.sent_at at connect, Heartbeat.sent_at thereafter). Add `received_time` to the hub UsageReading. Additive.
verify: critic (verified in files by the critic)
resolution: Hub is the time authority (02i "Clocks"): received_time on everything, one skew source (Hello.sent_time then Heartbeat.sent_time, median of 5), hub-adjusted time clamped to received_time for future stamps, cross-machine ordering by adjusted read_time with received_time tie-break, clock_untrusted above 15 min. hub UsageReading gains received_time and agent_read_time; MachineTelemetry.clock_untrusted; 02-contracts, W1 and 03b aligned.

title: Docs promise hub-to-agent traces, but Command, Event and Settings carry no trace context
evidence: docs/specs/03e-settings-and-drift.md:134-136 and 03c-goals.md:183-186 (spans `hub.settings.publish` to `agent.settings.merge`, `hub.scheduler.plan` to `hub.command.send` to `agent.start_goal`, `hub.drain` to `agent.drain`); docs/adr/0001-system-architecture.md:60 (OTEL traces from the first version); agent/v1/command.proto:24-84 (Command envelope has no trace field); grep 'trace' in api/: none.
problem: All commands ride one long-lived Connect stream, so per-RPC gRPC metadata cannot propagate a W3C traceparent per command. Without an envelope field the cross-process spans in the workflow docs cannot be linked. Correlation falls back to command_id attributes only.
fix: Add `string traceparent` (W3C) to Command, and to Event or CommandResult for the reverse direction. Document it as optional and capped at 55 bytes. Additive.

title: Opaque ids are used as tmux names, env values, file paths and resource keys with no format rule; StartGoal's new-session name is ambiguous
evidence: agent/v1/command_goal.proto:113-114 ('empty = new session named by the hub in spec.session_id'; StartGoal has no name field) vs agent/v1/command_tmux.proto:67 (names must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}) and :17-35. type/v1/ids.proto:45-53 (SessionId and GoalId go into FLEET_SESSION_ID and FLEET_GOAL_ID). hub/v1/settings.proto:49-50 (resource id 'group/<label>' with labels as free strings up to 256 bytes). docs/specs/03d-triage-sessions-logs.md:287 (log files keyed by session).
problem: Nothing defines id generation (ULID, length, charset). A session id used as the tmux session name must satisfy the 32-character name regex, and ids end up in environment values, file names and `group/<label>` keys that break if a label contains '/'. Developers will make different choices in the hub and agent in week one.
fix: Add an ids rule to 02-contracts: all hub-assigned ids are lowercase Crockford ULID or a stated prefix plus 26 chars, [a-z0-9-] only, at most 32 chars. Give StartGoal an explicit `session_name` (or state that the name is derived from the id and window template). Restrict group labels to the same charset. Additive.

resolution: ids.proto header: hub-assigned ids are 1 to 32 characters of [a-z0-9-] (lowercase ULID), user-chosen names that land in tmux names, env values, paths or group keys are [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}; PrincipalId is the documented exception.
